## **Chapter 1 – “A Dream of Self-Satisfaction” / “Delusion of Dependence”**

![A cartoon of a child lying downAI-generated content may be incorrect.][image2]

Tiat knew she was powerful from the start.

Of course, they'd fought back and forth during training, mostly as equals. But there were two simple reasons for this. One was that it was a training environment for mutual improvement, and it was impossible to display a strength that could reduce an opponent to ash. The other reason lay in her own personality. Lakish Nyx Seniolis’ personality was gentle, valued her friends, peaceful, and timid, completely at odds with her talents.

So, it was only natural that after she shed these two shackles, Lakish would transform into a weapon far beyond her normal self—a powerful weapon that Tiat Shiba Ignareo could never hope to match.

The first clash, then the second. Every time their swords met, she was helplessly overwhelmed. Tiat was unable to fully resist the opponent's attack. The pressure exerted by the Lakish’s Venenum was simply a different level. The opponent's overwhelming strength disregarded any factors that might be considered clever, such as swordsmanship, physique, and weight. There was a fundamental gap between them.

"La…"

Lakish, why? She wanted to ask. But there was no room for words between her breaths. She couldn't open her mouth to loosen her clenched teeth. If she didn't focus her entire attention on the "enemy" before her, she might not even be able to stand.

No, it was more than that.

Just the current state was already reaching her limit. The opponent effortlessly raised Seniolis and swung it. She couldn't dodge, barely managing to block the sword's path with Ignareo, avoiding a direct blow.

—But the sword's blast carried an explosive force that she couldn't withstand. She was literally sent flying like a pebble batted by a club.

—Ahh…

The scenery shifted endlessly, a dizzying sight.

Tiat flew through the air like a cannonball, her mind racing with thoughts.

For example, the sadness of being at war with her cherished family; the joy that welled up at the sight of her spirited presence, no matter what form she took; the anger at why she inexplicably decided to follow Feodor; and finally, the humiliation of being helplessly sent flying by her, caught in such a predicament. Tiat pushed the countless tangled fragments of her mind into a corner. Since crashing into a tree at this rate was dangerous, she calmly decided she needed to defend herself. She wiped the tears from her eyes and was about to force herself to regain her composure in mid-air when…

There was a soft thud.

Something soft and powerful… someone's arm caught her firmly.

"—Huh?"

She was confused, her thoughts frozen.

"You did well."

A voice Tiat knew all too well whispered softly.

—Huh…huh?

It was a voice she missed so deeply, a voice she had once loved most, a voice she had always listened to with longing, a voice she would never hear again, a lost voice.

Tiat raised her head, trying to confirm the person's face. But until the previous battle, she had been pushing her body too hard, and it no longer obeyed her heart's commands. She stared at Lakish as she approached her calmly, without moving further.

"Could it be… senior…"

Why couldn't a Leprechaun’s eyes look directly behind her? She twisted her stiff neck to its limit, straining her eyes to tilt upward. Even then, she couldn't see the other person, not even a hair.

"Hmm."

Only a soft, affirmative voice echoed in her ears.

"But why…"

"I couldn't bear to leave you, so I came back. You see, I'm not the only one."

A slender finger pointed straight ahead from behind Tiat. Another figure appeared in the direction the finger pointed, inserting itself between Lakish and Tiat.

"Hey, Tiat and Lakish, long time no see."

She saw the silhouette of a tall man, his profile. It was the face of someone she deeply… no, rather, someone she still somewhat missed, still somewhat fond of, still somewhat reliable, but also someone she would probably never see again.

"What the hell, it's only been a while since we last met, and you two have already grown so tall? Those so-called growth periods really are terrifying, huh?"

The voice was completely devoid of tension.

The man crossed his arms, nodded affirmatively, and turned back to Lakish.

"Who… who are you two?"

Lakish, naturally startled by the two uninvited guests, cried out in bewilderment. However, the man, unfazed, approached the girl at a leisurely pace.

Danger\! Tiat thought.

The Lakish now was no longer the innocent and simple girl they had known.

Lakish, influenced by a certain bad man, had transformed into a completely different person. She was in the midst of a dangerous rebellious phase, ready to destroy everything she came into contact with. Furthermore, she could wield the incredibly powerful and ominous superweapon, the Dug Weapon Seniolis. The two newcomers, who were supposedly not here, or rather, hadn't existed for five years, wouldn't know any of this.

And, as she'd predicted, after finally recovering from her confusion, Lakish raised Seniolis with a merciless aura and swung it at the approaching man—

"Huh?"

The wind whistled as the sword cut through nothing but air.

"Huh?"

Tiat, oblivious to her own situation, let out a dumbfounded cry.

She'd assumed it was a fatal blow, impossible to dodge at this distance. At least if it were her, she probably wouldn't realize what had happened until her head was parted from her body and sent flying. But…

"Hahaha\! You seem as spirited as ever. I'm relieved in every way." I don't know how the man dodged the previous blow, but I saw him standing behind Lakish.

"That sword strike was brilliant, without a trace of hesitation. Using this technique with Seniolis, it is without peer… But, despite that\!"

The man gave a pretentious, sly smile and pointed firmly at Lakish.

"Only a father's love would not be shattered by such a strike\!”

“…………”

What is this guy talking about?

Faced with this truly unexpected development, Tiat's mind went blank.

"Come on, Lakish\! Although your body is in a state of utter devastation due to various reasons, I will physically endure these few words of rebellion\!"

"So, what the hell’s going on with you two people?"

Lakish's voice was once again bewildered—and tears were mingled with her voice. The man didn't take it seriously. He leaped to his feet, arms spread wide, a "come hug\!" look.

"Take this\! Emnetwyte Secret Technique—The Fist That Absolutely Crushes Fatherly Love\!"

What kind of name is that? What's he trying to crush?

"Slow down, slow down, slow down. What's with that joint?"

"Wow\!" His entire body was twisting, twisting so much that it was hard to say if it was even physically possible for a living thing to twist like that.

"Wow, hahahaha, don't even think about escaping, my daughter\! Watch me\!"

"Wow\!" He flew up.

"Aaaaaah, so disgusting, so disgusting\! Twisting and turning is disgusting\!"

Mm, it was truly disgusting. Tiat just couldn't bear it. 

"Bonds can easily transcend common sense and the laws of physics\! Come, let love envelop you, open your heart\!"

*What the hell has this person been saying all this time?* "Bonds aren't like that\! We should pay attention to common sense\!"

Ah, that scream always sounded like the old Lakish.

It was truly bizarre.

What was going on? What was going on? She saw everything unfolding before her eyes, but she couldn't comprehend a single thing.

In this state, Tiat's mind went blank. She could do nothing but stare blankly with her mouth agape—

Just then, she woke up.

"…………"

She sat up abruptly in bed.

Roughing her tangled hair, she glanced at the morning light streaming in through the slits in the curtains, gently rubbed her slightly puffy eyes, and then yawned loudly.

"………………"

She stared blankly at the morning light for a long moment…

"What on earth was that dream?" Tiat whispered (so as not to wake the others in the dorm), then clutched her head with all her might. 

## **Chapter 2 – “Hunting down that criminal, then…” / “Who is tagger?” /**

### **Part 1 – The Fifth Division on That Day**

It is said that the surface of the earth was once a fertile land.

However, the then-thriving human race created the Seventeen Beasts and unleashed them. These Beasts, various in form, were the embodiment of destruction, annihilating humanity and most of the inhabitants of the earth in a flash.

After a long period of flight, the surviving inhabitants, guided by the Great Sage, reached the heavens. Because the Seventeen Beasts were wingless, they could not directly attack the inhabitants who left the surface.

Over five hundred years have passed since then.

These five hundred years have been shrouded in a precarious peace. They have repeatedly faced threats of destruction, barely repelling them and surviving to this day.

The present-day floating continents of Regul Aire are built on the accumulation of miracles.

The day of reckoning is approaching.

In recent days, the Fifth Division of the Winged Guard has had a great deal of work to do. The enormous menace, the Croyance, the Eleventh Beast, now inching closer to the island, once a friendly neighbour, is now approaching. The Winged Guard must urgently devise a countermeasure. The Beasts are inherently immortal, making them impossible to defeat with ordinary weapons. Until now, the Winged Guard have primarily used massive, conventional weapons to halt their movements and then shoot them down from the islands. The only common weakness shared by all the Beasts (as far as we know) is their lack of wings, making them incapable of independently ascending to the floating continents. Therefore, there's no need to insist on killing such immortal beings; expelling them from the sky is the most appropriate and practical solution. However, the Croyance, now enveloping the entirety of Floating Island 39, is no longer feasible. To destroy it, the enveloped island itself may have to be blasted to dust. However, Floating Island 39 was a vast island, and the Eleventh Beast, covering it, protected the rocky surface like armour. Using ordinary weapons and tactics would be difficult to even chip away at a small piece of the surface. Unless they employed exceptionally powerful weapons or tactics that defied common sense, they would be completely helpless.

The destruction of the giant strategic vessel "Utica" was a significant loss. The Mountain Thrower, aboard the Utica, was the strongest and heaviest weapon currently available to the Floating Islands. With the Mountain Thrower, perhaps they could have broken through the protection of the Eleventh Beast and shattered Floating Island 39\. Even if that outcome wasn't achieved, the extent of the damage inflicted by the Mountain Thrower attack would still provide the most effective clues for planning the next offensive. At least the powerful leaders of the Winged Guard were likely considering this.

However, the strategically important warship was no longer there. It was swallowed up by the "Stagnant Eleventh Beast" in a place unrelated to Floating Island 39, vanishing from the surface. Naturally, more than half of that ship was the product of the technicians' whimsical creation, and its manufacturing cost was unmatched by other ships—thus, a replacement was not easily feasible.

The nearest Winged Guard base was bustling with activity more than ever.

Preparations were being made tirelessly for the approaching battle.

Supply boats were constantly entering and exiting the harbour area, bringing in supplies. Previously closed civilian factories were being purchased one by one and converted into production facilities for new weapons.

And then, everyone was busy running around, each carrying a large amount of supplies, equipment, and instructions. At this time, racial differences were no longer a factor, not even between lieutenants and enlisted personnel.

All of them faced the impending battle, and shared a common sense of crisis, so they all worked together to prepare for it.

In some ways, it was a scene of profound fairness and equality. After moving nearly all the heavy boxes, they took a short break. Their entire body was warm to the perfect temperature. Even though they'd used a little magic to strengthen their bodies, manual labour still required the use of their muscles. Their upper arms and thighs were tense; they'd probably be experiencing mild muscle aches tomorrow. Tiat Shiba Ignareo went to the restaurant and ordered some ice-cold water, then stepped under the shade of a tree. Listening to the cool rustling of leaves, she tilted the container, letting the water wash away the foreign sensation deep in her throat.

"Huh."

She took a breath, calming herself… But the next moment, a flush of heat washed over her face.

"Ugh… Ahhhhh\!"

She remembered her dream from that morning. It was a deeply embarrassing one. She had indeed engaged in a swordfight with the drastically altered Lakish, and due to the disparity in power, she was no match for her, being beaten to the point of being unable to fight back. So far, there was nothing wrong with that. Setting aside the tragic nature of the dream, there was nothing wrong with having it in itself.

The problem lay in what happened next.

The encouragement and help she received from someone whose voice she longed for, the inexplicable support she received, were all her own delusions. Whenever a memory of reality she didn't want to accept was brought to her, her mind automatically filled in the "I wish it had happened this way" scenario. It was a dream that blatantly displayed her own desires, with a host of childishly distorted elements.

Willem Kumesh—their "father"—was portrayed as a rather foolish character in her dream. Perhaps that was how he appeared to her in her youth. In reality, he wasn't so abnormal, strange, or illogical. Perhaps. “Wuwu-“, her head throbbed.

The point is, even now, she's still like a spoiled child, having made no progress at all.

She'd risen up as a capable soldier, blocking Feodor's path, engaging in a swordfight with Lakish, and then been utterly defeated. It would have been fine if it had ended there, but in her dream of defeat, she was aided by her guardian. How else could that be explained? Doesn't that mean she's still the same child, unconsciously hiding under someone's protection, her mindset completely unchanged?

In the end, that's all she's become. She idolised those handsome adults, hoping one day to be like them, working hard and noisily, even receiving unexpected praise from senior Aiseia, saying she was excellent. Despite this, deep down, she still wanted to leave everything she couldn't do to the great seniors and the others.

Yes, that desire was so strong that it even caused her to have that dream.

"Wuwuwu—\!"

She clutched her head, twisting her body from side to side. "What's wrong? You've been acting so strangely again today, really attracting attention." A familiar voice reached her ears.

She snapped back to her senses and quickly stood straight.

Now was no time to squirm around because of reminiscence. She had much else to do, things she needed to dwell on. Time was limited, so she couldn't dwell on the past. She needed to focus on the present moment and the future ahead. And so she thought about all these things.

Standing before her was a girl of about her age, with lavender hair—Panival Nox Katena, who seemed curious.

"Are you thinking about Feodor?"

"No…" She thought for a moment. "No\!"

She wasn't lying. She hadn't been thinking about that guy.

In fact, Feodor himself hadn't appeared in the dream. Although he was one of the reasons for the conflict between her and Lakish, and a crucial figure, he simply wasn't there.

"Then could you do me a favour? Today seems to be a particularly busy day for messengers. I'm running around delivering documents, and I'm completely overwhelmed." Panival shook the bag slung over her shoulder.

"…I just finished a job and need a break."

"I suppose so. But being active keeps your mind from wandering."

Hmm. She didn't know how to respond. As expected of a long-time friend, Panival had already seen through her every thought.

…While it might be because her personality was easy to understand, she decided not to dwell on it.

"Here are these and this for you. Please send them to the head commander as quickly as possible."

"Oh, how shameless\!"

Tiat accepted the thick and heavy bundle of documents. "I'm just not really eager to see the commander-in-chief, the First Officer."

"Really, why not? What happened? You didn't say, 'I'll definitely defeat you next time we meet,' because your plot failed, did you?"

"How could that be possible? I'm not Panival.”

"No, I wouldn't do something so lacking in common sense."

"Then why do you say that?" Tiat swallowed the urge to point it out and said, "Well, it was when Feodor escaped. I pushed him several times, asking him to let me go after Feodor, but of course he wouldn't let me. It's been a bit awkward ever since."

While her words were true, her choice of words wasn't quite precise.

Precisely because it had been a while since the incident, now that her mind had calmed down, she realised the seriousness of the situation. Her actions during those few days couldn't be dismissed simply by saying, "I pushed him several times." Even if the commander-in-chief wanted to put her in solitary confinement to calm her mind, she couldn't complain. "The commander-in-chief is a generous man and won't take it to heart, so just let it go."

"That's true."

But it was precisely because she was so worried that she was so troubled. She felt sorry for causing trouble for the commander-in-chief. Furthermore, she had gone to great lengths to demonstrate her devotion to Feodor, a fact that made her feel ashamed.

"It's no big deal. Actually, I didn't want to meet him, and my shame is even more recent than yours."

"…What did you do?"

"It's nothing worth mentioning. At least it wasn't a backstabbing." Panival said, shrugging her shoulders nonchalantly. "When challenging an opponent, you must attack head-on. That's one of my mottos."

What on earth had she done?

 

†

 

The massive block of steel rolled over the thick rails, making a deafening "boom, clatter, clatter, clatter" noise as it moved. An extra-large armoured vehicle carries an ultra-large cannon. If the shells were fired directly, the vehicle would overturn due to the recoil, so several custom-made spades were added. However, this made it too heavy to travel on normal roads, so it was designed to run only on specialised iron rails. Thus, this thing was born.

It's called the "Ingus Marleo," the Boar-class Tracked Artillery Vehicle. With exceptional range and destructive power, its ground-based bombardment can even bring down large airships, making it one of the most useless weapons in the Regul Aire. 

…Exactly. While it can indeed bring down large airships, in other words, it's practically useless beyond just that. Furthermore, since it can only be used on tracked terrain, it must be used where the army's engineers can perform their duties perfectly. In other words, it's a "decisive weapon, essentially only effective in urban defense battles against strategic airships." In reality, such an opportunity is unlikely to occur. Rather, it would be troublesome if such opportunities arose frequently.

"With the current state of the war, even that kind of thing has to be dragged out…"

An Armado in officers’ uniform grumbled with emotion as he wiped the sweat from his brow.

"What did you just say?"

Next to him, a Haresanthropos military policeman in officers’ uniform—seemingly unable to bear the clatter of the artillery vehicles, slightly lowered his slender ears—exclaimed.

"No, just a complaint\! I think former Fourth Officer Feodor is truly capable\!" The First Officer shouted back. "I only realised how important he was after he was gone\! I had no idea that just without him, the daily workload would increase\! I'm on the verge of tears\!"

"Now's not the time for such carefree talk\!"

The military policeman pressed his forehead as if trying to suppress a headache. "You haven't forgotten what mischief that capable former officer Feodor got into, have you?"

"Even if you say so\! I've only really uncovered a fraction of what he was planning\! After all, you won't tell me what else he's done\!"

"We're not trying to embarrass you\! It's just that even now, we still haven't been able to fully grasp his full plan\!"

The artillery vehicle stopped with the sharp sound of steel braking.

Then, several spades unfolded, anchoring the vehicle to the ground. Perhaps because the noise had died down and he had calmed down a bit, the military police officer rubbed his outer ears gently and muttered to himself in a low voice:

"We've checked his private room, even the floorboards, and even conducted a character investigation at the bakery he frequents—it's not entirely fruitless, we did get a lot of information we didn't know before—but even that still doesn't give us a clear grasp of what he wants or what he's planning."

"In other words, even if he failed, he's not completely defeated."

The sound tickled his nose, and he scratched it lightly with his fingertips.

"He even considered the possibility of a fatal mistake somewhere, spreading the risk across multiple areas. So, even if a mistake did occur, it wouldn't be a complete failure. His talent truly lies in such unassuming places."

Feodor Jessman was a cautious young man.

This was because he came hailed from Imp lineage, a tribe renowned for their strategic talents… or perhaps there was more to it than that. He doesn't rely on his youth or talent for arrogance. His actions are driven by a strong sense of purpose, allowing him to completely suppress his inner feelings and focus on the next step with precision. This is how he's survived.

At least, he was like this about a month ago.

However, recently—after meeting those four certain First-Class Equivalent Soldiers—he's become a little lax.

Perhaps because he's always lived a diligent life, he seems a little overwhelmed by the fact that his true self has been dragged out.

Thus, he's executing his carefully prepared plans ahead of time, volunteering for high-profile special missions, and making mistakes he would never have made in the past.

Has something changed him? However, a military officer wouldn't be so tactless as to question such matters. "…Once you're drawn to a life attitude so completely different from your past, you can't continue to be a death warrior. I won't say who I'm talking to at this point."

"Huh?"

"Nothing, I'm just talking to myself."

In the corner of his vision, several technicians were arguing loudly. Apparently, one of their struts had a slight bend…about the thickness of a scale, to be exact. "Who's in charge of repairs?" "Is the workshop door still open?" "Can't we just force it?" "You idiot\! It's bent like that, one shot will break it\!" "So steel has nerves more delicate than your wife." "What did you say?" "Very convincing." The heated exchange of words went on and on.

The First Officer turned his back on the commotion.

He still had a few areas he wanted to inspect today, or rather, while the sun was shining, so he had no time to waste.

"So that's what the report say? Does it mean to mobilise the military police to hunt him down, or does it mean we have absolutely no clue about that guy's whereabouts?"

"No, there are two leads on that front."

Hmm?

The First Officer paused at the unexpected words. "The first clue is that he seems to be receiving assistance from the Orc network. They're numerous and scattered across every city in the Floating Islands. With their support, it's unlikely that Feodor Jessman will continue to lurk within Lyell City, as evading the Winged Guard’s surveillance and leaving this island would be a simple task."

"…That's not necessarily true." He muttered his disagreement softly.

"That kid seems to have other plans in this city."

It's unclear if the military policeman heard him, or if they just ignored him. Regardless, the military policeman continued unconcerned. "The second clue is based on the first. About three days ago, several individuals, possibly disguised, boarded a trading vessel affiliated with the Tangerine Garnet Merchants and left the island. While there are no direct witnesses, we've confirmed several grounds that suggest one of them is Feodor Jessman."

"Oh?"

"Last night, that individual boarded another trading vessel in the harbour area of ​​Grimzel City, Floating Island 28\. Since he presented a local trade permit, we couldn't question or detain him, but we know his destination."

"Oh, well done."

Except for a very few species with strong wings, traveling between floating islands requires airships. And airships can only dock and depart in specially equipped areas. Therefore, the Winged Guard’s primary principle in hunting wanted criminals is to establish a surveillance network in the various harbour areas. Wanted criminals, of course, are aware of this and will always try every possible means to circumvent the surveillance network. Floating Island 28 is one of the most prosperous in the area, and its harbour area is quite large.

Furthermore, the security isn't particularly good, and the inspections of airships and passengers aren't strict—indeed, there are several ways to exploit loopholes.

"You did a great job, so please retract your previous statement."

"Ah—yes, yes, that's what I said about you having no idea of ​​their whereabouts. So you're actually concerned about it?"

As if another manoeuvre test was about to begin, the artillery vehicle restarted with a roar and vibration. Amidst the noise, the First Officer of the military police muttered, "I didn't expect you to care about such a small matter."

"What did you say?"

"No, nothing. So, where is that former Fourth Officer whose hidden agenda we couldn't even detect—"

"—Huh?"

The girl's voice brought their conversation to a halt.

They turned to look. "Could it be First Officer Baroni Makish?"

A young Faerie soldier, a Markless creature with flowing grass-coloured hair, was seen running towards them.

"Is it Tiat Shiba Ignareo?"

The fairy murmured, confirming her name.

"Ah, it's Mr. Baroni Makishi after all."

The girl came running over with brisk steps and said, "Long time no see. Ah, it doesn't seem like it's been that long, but even so, it still feels like a long time since I last saw you. What brings you to a place like this?"

"A place like this? You little girl…"

The commander-in-chief of the 5th Division of the Winged Guard, who resided on Floating Island 38, muttered softly. "I'm here to personally inform you of a few things. However, I plan to fly off to the other floating islands shortly."

"Wow, you're still incredibly busy."

"How pathetic."

"Ahaha, thank you for your hard work."

In terms of military power, capital, and authority, the Winged Guard is a powerful organisation. Furthermore, power must be constantly controlled—and sometimes, even under control, it can spiral out of control.

This rabbitfolk, Baroni Makishi, is a First Officer of the military police. His primary responsibility is to monitor and supervise the Winged Guard internally, responding to situations where control seems to be out of control. His "busyness" indicates that the Winged Guard is currently in a highly unstable state.

"Ah, by the way, er, commander-in-chief, I have something for you. I've been instructed to deliver it as quickly as possible, so please take a look at it immediately."

"Ah—yes, yes, even I, a commander-in-chief, feel incredibly busy. I wish someone could be gentle and considerate."

"While you emphasize this point, it seems like you'd be fine with just leaving it alone."

"I'm so happy to be trusted like that." The Armado chuckled, a bit self-deprecatingly, as they took the folder.

"Then I'll take my leave."

"Ah, don't go. Wait a moment."

Tiat was about to turn on her heel when she heard this and stopped.

"What's the matter?"

"Tiat, you've arrived just in time. Come listen to what this rabbit has to say."

"…Hmm?"

"Huh?"

"Huh?"

Baroni and Tiat looked at each other. "What happened?"

"Is this okay? If we continue talking about what happened just now, we'll touch upon a lot of secrets."

Their gazes shifted to the Armado.

"Besides, this little girl isn't completely unrelated to that person, is she? Involving someone with an unbalanced perspective would be very troublesome, wouldn't it?"

"That's why I asked her to join. Playing cold guesses with that guy won't lead to good results. Whether it's trying to corner him or arrest him, if we don't throw in a factor that can disrupt our calculations, we won't even stand a chance of defeating him."

Neither of them specifically mentioned a specific incident, but if they'd mentioned anything similar, Tiat could guess what they were talking about.

"Um, aren't they talking about…"

"Hmm, it's probably what you're thinking."

The Armado nodded readily and looked at Baroni Makish. "There's really nothing I can do. Since speculation has reached this point, there's no point in keeping it secret. So, I'll have to borrow the Dug Weapon's suitable Leprechaun, Tiat Shiba Ignareo, for a while."

"Please… can you find an officer to oversee it? The Dug Weapon user."

"Fortunately or unfortunately, there's someone perfect for the job. While the person involved will undoubtedly complain, I'm sure they'll eventually compromise."

"That's good. Please continue—"

Gnacking, gacking, gacking—the wheels rubbed against the rails, creating a deafening, intense noise that suddenly bombarded the three of them.

They all frowned, waiting for the unpleasant vibrations to fade from their teeth.

"—Please continue what you were saying."

"Okay."

Though Baroni’s ears twitched nervously, he cleared his throat and resumed the conversation. "The fugitive, Feodor Jessman, a former Fourth Officer, has escaped this floating island under the guidance of the Tangerine Garnet Merchants. We've confirmed that he and his fellow escapees, Lakish Nyx Seniolis, passed through Floating Island 28 and headed towards a more distant city."

"Have you found them?" Tiat couldn't help but interrupt, but Baroni didn't respond.

"However, the accuracy of this information is questionable, and the military police can't send out pursuit troops under the guise of a legitimate mission at this time."

"Huh… how could this be\!"

"Alright, calm down," the Armado said leisurely. "Brother Baroni, don't keep us in suspense. Let's get straight to the point. This girl is incredibly straightforward now, and beating around the bush won't work."

"Huh?" She thought to herself: What does this mean?

Baroni adjusted his glasses with his fingertips and continued, "…We can't send pursuers under the guise of a regular mission, but we can find another excuse. There's a rather complex and difficult situation happening there right now. While they haven't requested assistance, it's still possible to intervene and show some concern."

Uh, so what should we do? Seeing Tiat's expression of obvious confusion, Baroni lowered his eyes slightly, as if giving up.

"What I mean is, we can send you there through another mission. While your movements will be significantly restricted, it's better than staying far away and unable to do anything."

Tiat's eyes widened.

"The location is Floating Island 11, Harbor Block 1\. This city isn't completely unfamiliar to you, is it?

Neither the military police nor the Fifth Division can provide assistance, but you'll have to cope with it."

She blinked. "Number 11… Huh? The so-called Harbor Block 1, isn't that…"

"Well, it's a rather famous location, and one that you must have a special connection to personally.

Not only is it one of the few ancient capitals of the Regul Aire, but it's also the birthplace of the 'Elpis Incident,' and now caught up in another turmoil…"

The military policeman paused, finally naming the place.

"I'm referring to the city of Collinadiluche.”

### **Part 2 – Feodor Jessman**

A man he didn't recognize appeared on the other side of the mirror.

It sounded like a story about adolescent delusions, but it was the truth, and he couldn't help it. As Feodor studied the figure in the mirror, the person in the mirror, who looked nothing like him, also studied his face.

It was a tall, slender, black-haired, black-eyed, unmarked man, dressed in a black military uniform, with a face devoid of sharpness.

He didn't recognize this face—though Feodor wanted to say so, the truth was not. He had only just seen this face a few days ago, in shock. That day, inside the “pickle barrel” (Secret Warehouse Zero), he had opened a wooden box labelled "Dead Black Agate", mistaking it for the remains of the Shiantor, the First Beast. Feodor saw the man's body inside, seemingly asleep. 

"—Who are you…?"

Feodor, fighting back a headache, thrust his fist into the mirror.

The man in the mirror did the same.

"Who are you…?"

After a moment's delay, the man in the mirror echoed the question.

"I'm asking you\!"

"I'm asking you\!"

"Answer my question\!"

"Answer my question\!"

It went on and on.

The other person was simply imitating him. He felt like someone constantly questioning and answering an empty jar. The words he spoke bounced back, twisted, and then echoed back a moment later. He averted his gaze from the mirror. Repeating pointless actions would yield no results, not to mention only worsening his headache.

—This was a real headache.

This was clearly a symptom of hallucination. First, it was certain that he had peered into the chest containing the "Dead Black Agate". Then there was the fact that he had accidentally made eye contact with the person inside. Could he have been under some kind of curse in that moment? Or perhaps the Imp Eyes… though Feodor himself didn't fully understand, it was likely some powerful hypnotic power… that had gotten out of control, exerting a strange influence on his mind. He didn't know the answer, nor did he have the energy to calmly investigate the cause.

He felt like he had become quite useless in a short period of time.

A Fourth Officer, once a highly skilled and promising officer, had suddenly developed terminal hallucinations and was now a wanted criminal. It was truly tragic, almost comical. However, for a Markless race associated with vice and depravity, this was perhaps a standard way of life.

"Huh."

He took out his glasses, which had no prescription, and put them on.

Then he looked in the mirror. This time, the reflection was the familiar self he knew. For some unknown reason, the black-haired man's hallucinations seemed to only occur when he didn’t wear glasses. While this was only a temporary solution, it was a relief to have a solution. He decided to wear glasses whenever possible.

He glanced out the window, hoping to soothe his emotions.

The moss-coloured paint on the massive control wing was half peeling, and the emergency kite, perhaps unsecured, was dangling precariously.

And then, on the other side.

A sea of ​​clouds painted the lower half of his view a pure white, while the sky painted the remaining upper half a deep blue. "…………"

This was the airship belonging exclusively to the Tangerine Garnet Merchants, and he was staying in one of the guest rooms.

While it was a large airship designed for cargo, it certainly had a certain speed. However, the view from the window was like a picture stuck on, unchanged, a monochromatic palette of moss green, white, and blue. It quickly became tiresome.

Looking around the room, however, he found nothing particularly interesting. It was simply a renovated small warehouse. Besides the sofa bed he was currently sitting on, there was only a small wardrobe, a hippopotamus ornament, a wall clock, and the large mirror.

He glanced at the clock. It seemed they still had a while to reach their destination. Subconsciously, he followed the bird flying past the window with his eyes, recalling the events of a few days ago.

Feodor Jessman recalled the night he and Lakish had escaped from the Winged Guard and repelled the pursuing Tiat. He could still vividly remember the look on Giggir’s face when he told him he wanted to go to another floating island.

"I'm grateful for your help, and I'm sorry you've had to see me in such a hopeless state. In this situation, I hope you can lend me a hand… no, a leg."

Giggir asked him what his plans were.

"Don't you still have things to do on Floating Island 38?" he asked.

"Of course, the things I want to do are piled high as a mountain. However, the things I can do right now are so few, and the things I must do are another mountain."

His muscles and bones ached, protesting loudly, and the pain inside his eyes was no less intense. Feodor desperately suppressed his discomfort and spoke forcefully, "I've gathered enough intelligence here. The key to the Winged Guard’s weapons against the Primordial Beasts lies on the other floating islands. While losing my rank as a Fourth Officer is regrettable, the timing isn't too bad. After all, as long as I remain with the Winged Guard, I won't be able to do what I need to do now."

Giggir’s eyes were searching.

Feodor stared back.

He didn't feign expression, nor did he see the need. For right now, he only needed to make Giggir understand two things. First, his seriousness; second, his genuine belief in victory.

"We don't intend to wage war on our own. We simply want to share the Winged Guard’s exclusive military power and knowledge of the Beasts with the world. Therefore, focusing solely on the weapons themselves will be futile. What we need now is to find the facilities that produce and manage those weapons and identify the source."

He swallowed.

"To do this, I must rely on the assistance of Dr. Margomedari Brompton. He has expertise in various fields, including engineering, medicine, linguistics, and mysticism—"

"…You seem to be beating around the bush."

Giggir’s tone was skeptical. This wasn't surprising, after all. Giggir Mozag was a businessman, and a businessman isn't driven by vague dreams, but rather pursues practical profit.

"I'm asking directly: what benefits will our Tangerine Garnet Merchants gain from your approach?"

"As many people as possible will desire to learn about the Beasts. While I'd love to generously distribute this knowledge, I can't do that. The value of everything depends on the price paid. If information is simply presented without any effort and simply waited for, no one will recognize its value, so…"

"Oh, oh…"

The ugly pig face contorted even more.

"I see. So you want us to create an effect, to make everyone feel that this information is extremely valuable. And to achieve this, you want us to charge a huge fee."

"That's going too far."

Feodor chuckled. While the statement was admittedly unpleasant, the content was entirely correct. Giggir was absolutely right. "Next, we need the person you mentioned to facilitate this deal, am I correct?"

"That's right."

"Well, I think this is a worthwhile deal. Since I believe it's profitable, the people at Tangerine Garnet Merchants will continue to provide you with the utmost assistance."

"Thank you very much."

Giggir Mozag is a member of the Orc race. It's said that the Orc race is a very protective and insular race. Due to their short lifespan, they have developed a unique perspective on life and death, forming a closed community within their community, which has even caused friction with most other races.

Therefore—as long as both parties recognize a mutually supportive and equal relationship, they will never betray each other.

However, this doesn't mean they will always be so easygoing. Feodor had already inconvenienced Giggir and owed him a huge favour. So, from now on, he must continue to prove himself worthy of being an "equal partner" to this man.

*(Is this really okay?)*

He didn't ask the question. There were significant flaws in Giggir previous statement. For example, what was the connection between seeking doctor Margomedari and gaining knowledge of the Primordial Beasts? Furthermore, what was the specific process by which Feodor would convert his desired undertaking into money with Giggir’s assistance? The pig-headed man hadn't asked him any of these questions.

It was impossible for him to simply forget to ask; this man wouldn't be so careless. If that were the case, the only inference was that he had deliberately omitted the topic.

*(…For now, let's just accept his kindness.)*

For a thoughtfulness that hadn't been conveyed through words, he couldn't express his gratitude verbally. So, Feodor remained silent, his eyes slightly lowered.

"Then you…" At the last moment, when he had to confirm Lakish’s intentions, he became nervous. "Will you help me?"

"How could I possibly leave you?"

That was the girl's response. "I have nowhere to go and nothing to do, so I'll stay by your side, following my heart's desire. Whatever you decide to do, I'll support you, even if you don't agree." The girl, who had no memories of the past, said this, then smiled a childish smile—like a child adoring their parents.

*(…So, that's not the case.)*

The girl named "Lakish Nyx Seniolis" no longer existed. What's here is merely the fragmented "Lakish" personality, and the equally scattered fragments of her other personalities, miraculously reunited to form an imperfect and unstable mosaic.

Furthermore, the girl's yearning for Feodor wasn't a natural development. It was simply the result of Feodor's uncontrolled use of his unique eye power, the Imp Eyes, on this girl.

Precisely because of this, her thoughts had nothing to do with proper mental function.

There was no love or friendship between them, not even a mutual interest. "After all, you're my most important friend."

So he said, "Stop it. Stop sugarcoating it with those beautiful words."

Feodor gave an ambiguous smile, suppressing the urge to scream.

Accepting Giggir’s kindness.

Manipulating Lakish’s mind.

With nothing left of his own, Feodor could only shamelessly borrow the power of others, otherwise he would never be able to make a comeback.

 

†

 

The painkillers seemed to have worn off.

The excruciating pain from his leg injury forcibly interrupted Feodor's recollection, bringing his consciousness back to the airship.

"It hurts, it hurts so badly…"

This was the wound he had sustained when he fell into the underground of Lyell City a while ago, pierced by a metal pillar. Although he later received treatment and expected to recover with ten days of rest… the intense fighting and other events he'd experienced had completely reopened the wound, and even his muscles were aching all over again, seemingly by accident.

Of course, he had at least been promoted to the rank of Fourth Officer, and his accumulated combat training was more than worthy of that title. He also considered himself more tolerant of pain than most people… Even so, pain was still pain, and dislike was still dislike.

A knock on the door sounded beside him.

"Are you asleep?"

Without waiting for a response, the person outside turned the doorknob and pushed it open.

A girl with orange hair poked her head out from behind the door. Seeing Feodor standing by the window, she said with a hint of regret: "Oh, so you're awake."

"Why do you sound so regretful?"

"Because I do. If you were asleep, I could do whatever I wanted, right?"

"So what were you planning to do?"

"…Do you want to make a girl say it herself?"

"What exactly were you planning to do?"

The girl chuckled light-heartedly.

"I'm just kidding. How could I possibly do something you'd hate?"

"Who knows…"

Feodor muttered, his face twisting slightly. Waves of pain washed over him, sometimes stronger and sometimes weaker. Even if he didn't want to show it on his face, he couldn't keep his nerves tense. "Oh, come on. Okay, don't push yourself. I brought some painkillers."

"…Thank you so much."

"Besides, why are you still awake? Wounded patients should sleep well. And you look so pale. Don't you even notice?"

"Ahaha."

In reality, he'd been trying not to look in the mirror lately. But it was hard for him to say it out loud. So he just smiled and brushed it off.

"Okay, go back to bed. I'll take care of you."

"No, well… let's not do that. I'm a bit of a tough guy, and I don't want to show weakness in front of a girl…"

"Rejected."

He saw Lakish extend her fair hand, and the next moment, he felt like he was floating. Lakish picked him up and carried him to the bed as if she were carrying some lightweight cargo. "Lakish?\!”

"Your pretense is truly appalling. I can't bear to watch you. If you're going to preach your point, you should practice your acting skills more."

Feodor is an Imp.

The so-called Imps are not a kind race. They all enjoy devious schemes, lies, and the temptation to corrupt other races, and they excel at it. Tracing their lineage, it's said that they splintered from the evil human race back down on the land. While the truth of this claim is unclear, they are indeed so disliked that they've been spoken of to this extent.

Being associated with people like them is never a good thing. Their words and expressions cannot be trusted. This is floating on the widely held belief of Regul Aire. That's how it should be.

Thus, concealing his pretense wasn't particularly difficult for Feodor… that's how it should be. "Okay, lie down quietly, or do you want me to brute-force you?"

"I'll just lie down."

Feodor, surrendering his dignity as a man and the dignity of the Imps, tearfully obeyed Lakish’s command.

He lay down on the bed and let Lakish cover him with a blanket. He then shooed Lakish out of the room after she asked if he wanted a lullaby, and closed his eyes.

"…Alas."

There was still a little time left before reaching our destination.

In other words, with just a little more time, the boat would arrive safely.

Five years ago, a series of events occurred, now known as the "Elpis Incident."

It was the direct cause of the destruction of Feodor's homeland, the Elpis Mercantile Federation.

It was the fierce attack by two Beasts, the “Piercing Second Beast, Aurora" and the “Lamenting First Beast, Shiantor” that led to the destruction of the nation. Yet, the first and only city deeply affected by the disaster has managed to survive these storms.

"I've wanted to visit there before, but I never imagined it would be under these circumstances…"

—The distance to the city of Collinadiluche is growing closer.
