### **Part 3 – Reunion**

Speaking of which, Tiat Shiba Ignareo truly loves to create stories.

On Floating Island 68, not far from the Fairy Warehouse, owned by an Orc, there's a small, old Image Crystal Theatre. As a child, Tiat repeatedly begged the staff at the warehouse to take her there.

The Image Crystal, as its name suggests, is a special type of quartz that can capture and preserve the surrounding scene. Through the equipment in the Image Crystal Theatre, the scenes and stories sealed within can be revealed before one's eyes. Actors from all races perform a variety of dramas somewhere in the world. These dramas depict love, dreams, hope, and adventure. All of these fascinate Tiat immensely. Most plays are set in the city of Collinadiluche. So, just as Tiat once longed for those stories, she too once harboured a strong yearning for Collinadiluche.

However, Tiat now holds mixed memories of Collinadiluche.

As she soared through the skies in an airship, Tiat kept thinking about those events: that battle, that farewell.

The first event of the Elpis Incident, the day Collinadiluche was ravaged by the Beasts, Tiat was in the city, wielding Ignareo and participating in the first battle. In that battle—she was separated from Willem, the "father" of all the fairies.

"…Alas."

That was her favourite city as a child, a city she had always longed for.

Childhood longings must eventually come to an end. Tiat, now a full-grown fairy soldier, had learned to face reality to a certain degree, so she no longer shared the innocent excitement she once felt about fictional stories.

When she landed there, only sad memories would resurface, not the exhilaration she once felt.

That thought lasted only until she stepped off the airship's ramp.

"…Huh."

It seemed the longing once deeply embedded in her soul, though faded with time, wouldn't vanish so easily.

"Huh\!"

Floating Island No. 11, evening.

Tiat stepped off the airship's ramp, immersing herself in the bustling surroundings. The moment she breathed in the local air, an overwhelming surge of emotion welled up within her.

The city of Collinadiluche\!

A place where history converges\! A jewel box in the sky\! A medley of romance and legend\!

She suppressed the urge to scream. An endless stream of excitement surged through her body. It felt like if she wasn't careful, her skin would burst and explode at any moment.

"No, this shouldn't be happening."

Calm down, she thought, patting her cheeks.

This is a place of sad memories. I can't feel joy. Otherwise, well… should I say I'm sorry, Willem?

*"I'm not saying you can't cry even if you're sad. But don't use that as an excuse not to smile."* For some reason, suddenly, she thought of these words. *"You can laugh when you're sad, and you can cry when you're happy. Always cry and laugh with all your might. This is a child's privilege, and also their duty—"*

These were lines from a story she'd read before. An old killer, raising his granddaughter, repeated them repeatedly.

These words didn't come from Williem's mouth, but they sounded like something he would say. In Tiat's mind, Willem Kumesh was just that kind of person. He barely restricted or forced the younger Leprechauns into anything.

So, if he were here, he'd probably say something similar. She was certain of this.

"…Ahh, oh my\!"

She clutched her head, laughing and crying. And yet, she was left like this. What kind of heart was she supposed to have as she set foot in this place?

Many airships entered and exited the metropolis every day. Of course, most of them were tourists, cargo, and other miscellaneous goods. Airships, in principle, could only dock in well-equipped harbours. Therefore, the metropolis' harbours were constantly teeming with ships, day and night.

—That's right.

In the corner of her nearly shattered brain, she managed to use the few remaining fragments of rationality to reflect on the present.

She had to meet someone here.

Leprechauns weren't allowed to leave on their own. According to regulations, they couldn't go anywhere without supervision from a Winged Guard officer of the rank of lieutenant or higher. While this rule wasn't widely observed, it wasn't something to be taken lightly.

The Winged Guard cruiser that had brought her here left the harbour immediately after unloading its cargo.

"I heard the supervisor this time would be waiting here…"

Hopefully, he'd be reasonable. All the supervisors Tiat had known, past and present, were soldiers who weren't prone to putting on airs. Regardless of their personalities, at least they didn't restrict her strictly and respected her as an independent individual. Having always met such people meant she'd been quite lucky so far. As for the future, she might not always be so lucky.

She thought, glancing around. But she didn't see any uniforms that might have belonged to the supervisors.

"Excuse me—\! Excuse me—\!"

Several Orcs, carrying heavy wooden boxes, ran past Tiat, picking up a gust of wind. A gentle rustle of her bangs.

Standing nearby would be a nuisance, but she couldn't stray too far. Just as she hesitated about what to do…

"Ti—"

The voice grew closer.

"Tiat—\!"

It came from a blind spot.

With that cry, arms leaped over, enveloping Tiat's body in a tight embrace.

"Hmm?"

A surprised shriek blended with the air squeezed from her lungs, creating an eerie sound.

"What the hell, it really is Tiat? How come you've grown so much in just a while? Look at you\!"

The stranger clutched her, rocking her back and forth. Her vision blurred. She could see people on the street turning their heads, curiously glancing at her. It was truly embarrassing. It was embarrassing, but now, compared to this…

"Huh…"

She recognized the voice.

The forceful, powerful gestures were also incredibly familiar to her. Because years ago, in that nostalgic Fairy Warehouse, she'd seen this scene almost every day.

"Are you senior Noft?"

"Yeah\!"

The world suddenly stopped shaking, and she was held tightly.

She struggled to wriggle free, finally freeing herself. After a sharp gasp, she turned and finally saw the person.

She was a woman in her twenties, with crimson hair like maple leaves and eyes a shade darker than her hair. She was slender—standing upright, Tiat was a head shorter than her, forcing her to look up to meet her eyes.

She remembered a name—Noft Kei Oracion. She was one of the senior fairies who had left the Fairy Warehouse two or three years ago after accepting a special mission with the Winged Guard.

The person standing before her looked a lot like Noft. Her voice sounded like Noft’s, too. Besides, she had answered "yes" when her name was called earlier.

"Huh, but…?"

"Hmm?"

Her mind was already spinning, and now seeing the unexpected face, naturally, several questions popped up in her mind. After sorting them out, she decided to ask the most important one first.

"You've grown your hair out?"

"Oh, you're definitely paying attention to it. I originally thought cutting my hair was a hassle, so I left it alone. But Lan kept saying it suited me, so I started to seriously consider growing it out."

No, that wasn't the most important question.

"You've grown taller?"

"Only a little bit. You're exaggerating. That little girl has grown into a typical, well-to-do lady."

Noft chuckled wickedly.

Tiat felt like she'd seen that laugh before.

And this question, too, wasn't the most important one.

"Uh—" She calmed down. "—Why are you here?"

Yes, that's it.

That's the most important question to ask right now. The third challenge was finally a success.

"Hmm? What, you didn't hear?"

"I didn't hear anything. I was attacked by you all of a sudden."

"Oh, that's quite a disaster." Is that what the culprit responsible for this disaster should say?

"We only learned about it the day before yesterday, after returning from the ground. So, we flew directly here from Port 31."

The ground? In other words…

"Have you been on the surface? Until the day before yesterday?"

The surface. A lost paradise. A land of death and destruction ruled by the Seventeen Beasts. Countless lost ancient wisdoms lie dormant here, but many who seek to unearth them have paid the price with their lives… The surface is such a place. Furthermore, it is also the hometown of Willem Kumesh and the resting place of Kutori Nota Seniolis. "Don't be so surprised. Our Third Engineering Officer does just that kind of work. You should have heard about it from Naigrat, right?"

Naigrat was the Fairy Warehouse manager assigned by the Orlandri Trading Company. A Troll woman, she was like both a sister and a mother to all the Leprechauns.

"I've heard that. If I remember correctly, the Third Engineering Officer is the commanding officer of the surface survey troop. But that's not right. The surface isn't a place where you can easily come and go, right?"

"Yeah, about once every two months. Once you get used to it, it won't be so tiring."

"I don't think it's a place you can habitually go back and forth… ah, Mr. Engineer\!"

That's right. The shock of reuniting with Noft had almost made her forget. She now had to meet the lieutenant of the Winged Guard.

"Yes\!"

Noft smiled slyly and pointed behind her with her chin. "Hey, you little one, don't run off without permission, okay? I'll be the one getting scolded later—"

A short figure slowly emerged from behind Noft.

It was a green Borgle, dressed in a lieutenant's uniform. Remember, they were a type of Goblin, a race that, if you're honest, tended to be passive, conservative, and artistic.

"—I apologize for interrupting your warm and nostalgic reunion, little girl. Are you Tiat?"

"Ah, yes…" She had never seen this face before; it was undoubtedly their first meeting. Yet, she felt very familiar with this person.

Looking back, she must have heard stories about him often in the Fairy Warehouse. For example, he was a skilled salvage expert, having brought back several relic weapons from the surface. He was the one who discovered Willem and introduced him to the Fairy Warehouse. He was a witness to senior Kutori’s final battle. After the Elpis Incident, he joined the Winged Guard at their urging, becoming the head of the surface survey. Currently, senior Noft’s actual job is to serve as a guard for this person.

*I remember his name—*

"My name is Grick Graycrack. I'm grateful for your guidance."

Yes. He was Grick from the Graycrack clan. 

"Pleased… to meet you.”

Facing the dark green hand extended to her, she hesitantly and gently grasped it.

It felt rough, the hand of someone skilled in a certain craft. "Uh, my name is Tiat… Tiat Shiba Ignareo. Thanks for taking care of Senior Noft.”

"Haha\!" Glick turned around. "Look\! The younger sister is actually more polite. What about you?”

"Stop rambling\!"

They laughed heartily at each other.

"Is everyone in the warehouse okay?"

"Uh… sort of, for now."

"Is that so? Well, that's good."

Tiat remembered something. This senior Noft had once been the wielder of the Dug Weapon Desperatio and had been known as "Noft Kei Desperatio". However, that Desperatio was lost on the battlefield, and the sword's name vanished from her name along with it. Not long after that, she was given the opportunity to retrain. Formerly Noft Kei Desperatio, she had been found compatible with the Dug Weapon Oracion, becoming an adult fairy soldier named Noft Kei Oracion… That's how it should be.

"Senior, you look quite energetic, don't you?"

"Yes, after all, that's my only positive point."

Noft scratched her head, her long hair flowing gracefully.

What's this? Tiat wondered. Where had Noft, who used to have a boyish, short, unruly hair, gone? In other words, why was her hair so flowing? Tiat had naturally curly hair, and every morning she had to deal with messy hair from sleeping, so she felt she had every right to be jealous. What was going on?

"What's wrong?"

"Ah, no, it's nothing." Tiat felt a little embarrassed and looked away.

"How should I put it? I'm truly sorry. Even though I'm older than you, I couldn't help in that moment of need."

"Don't say that… It's all my fault." Tait said. Unable to shake off the embarrassment, she turned away.

"That's not true\!" Noft grabbed her head firmly from above. "You've always behaved well. No one can blame you\!"

Tiat's hair was ruffled violently.

She was a little angry. Noft had been away from the Fairy Warehouse for years. How much could she possibly understand about Tiat Shiba Ignareo?

Tiat was angry, but also a little amused. She was a little dumbfounded by her own naiveté. Cheer up, okay?

From here, it was a long way to the Winged Guard Commander's headquarters in the city of Collinadiluche.

The three of them walked side by side.

As they walked, they saw strange things scattered throughout the streets.

It was a hole. Amidst the otherwise unchanged streetscape, vast holes were dug into the stone slabs and walls. While all the holes had been repaired and sealed with new stone and plaster, restoring the streets to their former beauty proved difficult.

"What caused that?"

After Tiat asked, Noft scratched her head, seemingly at a loss for words. "It was the Second Beast that caused this. Five years ago, when the people of Elpis unleashed a large number of them, you were the ones who defeated them, weren't you?"

"Ah… well, we weren't the only ones."

"That's true. The soldiers of the Winged Guard fought with all their might. The Second Beast isn’t very sturdy, so there wasn’t apocalyptic. Even a standard gunpowder musket can destroy its form depending on how it's used."

Noft said "but" and continued:

"The Beasts don't understand death. After chopping and burning those creatures, their shattered forms will cling to the stone slabs, leaving black stains. But this isn't true death. After a while, they'll return to their original form and move again."

For a long time, the only forces that could effectively counter the threat of the Seventeen Beasts were the Dug Weapons—and the fairy soldiers who wielded them. It wasn't just their immense destructive power, but the death they inflicted through a magical power that contradicted the concept of life. Even the Beasts, who didn't understand death, couldn't ignore it… That's what they speculated.

"So, could it be…" Tiat gasped. So…

"Well, that's what happened. After a few of them resurrected, they caused a huge panic. We managed to clean up the mess, but if they continued to resurrect, it would have been disastrous. So everyone dug up the black stains, along with the stone slabs and walls, and dumped them over, down to the surface. It was a complete mess."

It was a mess. Tiat thought it was no wonder.

After all, the residents of this city were completely unaware of the threat posed by the Beasts—not just knowledge, but also no personal experience or feeling—and they had lived their lives in this way. Suddenly faced with a threat they had previously thought had no bearing on them, it was impossible for anyone to remain calm. "I feel like… people on the street seem so gloomy."

Tiat asked about something that had been bothering her. "Did that start that day, too?"

"No, about two years ago. The idea of ​​the Heaven’s Arrival was becoming popular then, so I guess that's probably why."

Heaven’s Arrival. It's a dangerous ideology with a long and profound history, even inseparable from the history of the Regul Aire. According to its content, the surface of the earth is filthy, while the sky, in contrast, is pure. We who left the surface must continue to pursue higher goals, so we must leave the land of the Floating Islands and sail to the distant stars—and so on. Using this excuse to induce people to commit suicide (purportedly liberating the soul)…

"So… that's how it is."

Tiat couldn't understand the thinking of those who held such a line of thought. Human life is inherently finite. Why would someone, in a situation where they are only allowed a certain amount of time, pursue something so ruthlessly assuring themselves of their own mortality? "That's so depressing."

"That's right."

However, even the most dazzling things will eventually fade. The city of Collinadiluche, which Tiat once longed for, won't retain its former glory forever. It's simply that simple.

 

"Is his name Feodor Jessman? The man the little girl is pursuing."

Grick, seemingly a little excited, changed the subject.

"He's an Imp? The brother-in-law of the deputy commander of the Elpis National Defence Force? He joined the Winged Guard and rose to the rank of Fourth Officer? And during that time, he meticulously planned a rebellion, only to fail and flee? This man's life is truly full of ups and downs."

"…Is that person something you can talk about so casually?"

Noft’s eyes, on the other hand, sharpened, her displeasure unconcealed. "You haven't forgotten what the Elpis National Defense Force did five years ago, have you? Since they're their remnants, and they're planning to do the same thing, this is both a tough and true enemy. This isn't something we can discuss with a smile, is it?"

Tiat lowered her head slightly, avoiding Noft’s gaze.

"That idiot is like that, but there's something different about him."

"Huh?"

"I can't really put it into words. He's a bad guy, but not truly evil. He's dangerous, but I don't think he'd do anything truly dangerous. Hmm…"

"Nope, I don't get what you’re saying at all."

Tiat thought so. She also didn't know what she was talking about.

"I don't fully understand, but I have a rough idea of ​​what kind of guy he is. And seriously, that expression you’re wearing… so, you’ve got that look too.”

"…Huh?"

"Look in a mirror, Tiat. It’s the same as hers back then.”

"Who?" Tiat wondered.

So she waited. However, Noft remained silent.

"But, hunting down that Feodor right now is going to be a bit of a hassle," Grick muttered, scratching his nose.

"Noft and I belong to the Second Division, and the little girl belongs to the Fifth. You're considered an outsider here. Since we're here as reinforcements to deal with the problems in this city, you can't just wander around."

"It's so troublesome. Can't you just ignore those rules?"

Glick smiled wryly. "Don't say that. I'm not young anymore. I can't act recklessly."

Of all the races inhabiting the floating continents, the Borgles have one of the shortest lifespans. They reach adulthood around twelve, begin to age around thirty, and reach the end of their lives around forty.

She didn't know the exact age of this Grick Graycrack, but since he'd said so himself, it meant he was quite old by Borgle standards. "Oh, I can't stand old people becoming so reserved and cautious."

"Whatever you say."

"…Um, excuse me, um, what are the problems in this city?" Watching the two bickering—though it seemed like a joke—Tiat timidly interrupted. "Actually, I haven't heard the details. I just know that the trouble here means you need an extra pair of hands."

"Oh, well, speaking of that…"

"Ah, sorry, I didn't think of that for a moment," Tiat apologized. "This kind of thing can't be discussed in public, so lets talk about it after we arrive at headquarters…"

Grick pondered for a moment, then lowered his voice.

"There have been four consecutive assassinations of key Winged Guard members recently."

"…Huh?"

"Listen up, Noft. We'd better finish discussing this before we arrive at headquarters."

"Huh?"

"That bastard, Baroni Makish, must have expected me to do this—Grick muttered something like a complaint, waving at the two. Noft and Tiat glanced at each other, then pressed their ears to the green officer’s mouth.

"All those killed were those responsible for tuning you fairies."

"—What?"

Seeing Noft about to shout, Tiat quickly covered her mouth.

Leprechauns appear in the world as children. Once they grow, they undergo special training and become adults, participating in battle as fairy soldiers wielding Drug Weapons. As an adult fairy soldier, Tiat had naturally undergone a so-called conditioning treatment. However, she couldn't quite recall the details… She was stripped naked and injected with several potions, which seemed to contain a mixture of sleeping and anaesthetic drugs, leaving her half-asleep for most of the conditioning process. Even when she asked the doctor who performed the conditioning, he simply said, "It's confidential," and refused to disclose.

It wasn't until recently that she understood something.

Leprechauns that appear as children would normally dissolve and disappear from the world as children. However, fairies that undergo conditioning can avoid this fate. They are allowed to exist as "adults," extending their lifespans. Conversely, without conditioning, young fairies would follow the normal path of fairies and die before reaching adulthood.

Furthermore, a problem has recently arisen.

For various reasons, the current Winged Guard leadership is cautious at the need for Leprechaun weapons. Because of this, the juvenile fairy soldiers currently stored in the Fairy Warehouse cannot be tuned.

A calm reflection reveals that this situation is temporary. For the Winged Guard, abandoning weapons like the Leprechauns offers little benefit.

Adult fairy soldiers are like a difficult-to-dispose-of bomb. Keeping multiple adult fairy soldiers around at once without a purpose carries enormous risks and comes with significant costs. Therefore, the reason for halting adjustments is likely to minimise unnecessary risk and cost, achieved by a reduction in the number of adult fairy soldiers in existence.

Given this, there's a strong possibility that tuning of the juveniles will resume in the future, to maintain a baseline readiness level. For example, several current adult fairy soldiers could die, reducing their numbers; or, perhaps, adult fairy soldiers, even though they're bombs, could prove to be highly effective weapons on the battlefield today. In this way, perhaps those children bracing for destruction in the warehouse could be offered a future of adulthood. Yes, Tiat Shiba Ignareo, Lakish Nyx Seniolis, Panival Nox Katena, and Collon Rin Purgatorio—the four of them volunteered to be sent to Floating Island 38 with this very thought in mind—

"Who… is it…" At that moment, her mouth went dry. "Who is it, and why would they do this?"

"If we don't consider too many factors, it's likely someone wants to irreparably damage the 'Fairy Soldier' ​​system. After all, even among the relevant personnel, it seems only a handful of people know the details of the Fairy Soldier's control. If they kill those few and successfully destroy the failsafe mechanism, it can easily disable the system. However, the truth is currently shrouded in mystery."

"Why?"

"Who knows? At this point, we don't have enough information, so it's hard to say. Furthermore, since the individuals being targeted are all connected to the Winged Guard’s secrets, it's highly likely that the enemy has some inside information. Therefore, everyone at headquarters is a little nervous."

"…Ah."

Noft made a sound of annoyance. "I can't stand it. Why is everyone so obsessed with schemes and scheming?"

"That's what I mean. People should live a simpler life, isn't that right, little girl?"

"Isn't that right?" Tiat chuckled, brushing it off. She really wanted Feodor to hear what she had just said.

"Anyway, that's what happened. Fortunately or unfortunately, we've already identified the next target. You know, he's someone you know well."

After a pause, Grick stated the man's name with mock solemnity.

"Dr. Margomedari Brompton."

Tiat blinked.

She searched her memory, but couldn't find the name or the corresponding appearance.

Uh…

"Who is he?" She and Noft asked in unison. 

\=====

### **Part 4 – The Young Man in the Black Suit**

**![][image4]**

The city of Collinadiluche. This ancient city was the most prosperous on Floating Island 11, and one of the most historic in all Regul Aire. Countless poets sang its praises of beauty, abundance, and glory. Many playwrights chose it as a stage for depictions of love, sorrow, honour, and folly.

Feodor was, to be honest, unfamiliar with aesthetics, but he felt a deep understanding of the power and mystique of love. Everyone lives and dies for love, achieving unimaginable successes and suffering utterly disastrous failures. Seeing the city of Collinadiluche rise to fame and continue to be loved by so many, the Imps, whose profession was to captivate people, even felt a kind of respect. But…

"—It's not quite what I expected." He whispered his true feelings.

The stone streets were painted in bright hues. Like a display of meticulously crafted boxes, this heartwarming scene was even endearing.

Hundreds of years must have passed behind these street scenes, and this rich history could be felt with one's own skin rather than through appearance.

One could imagine how beautiful this city once was.

One could imagine how beloved this city once was.

Of course, applying these two sentences to the present day wouldn't be wrong. However, compared to the city's former beauty and the way it was loved, the Collinadiluche before him now clearly lacked.

The reason for this thought was probably—

"Are you thinking about something?"

"…Ah, nothing." The question brought Feodor back to his senses.

Though he didn't intend to dwell on it, he seemed slightly distracted. He shifted his gaze a bit frantically, glancing left and right, instantly assessing the situation. It was past noon in the city of Collinadiluche, and he and Lakish were walking side by side through a narrow alley.

The city was vast, but not entirely touristy. Away from the crowded areas, one found a quiet residential area. The situation here was not unlike that of Lyell. In this city, even the residential areas should have a mysterious aura, radiating from centuries of history.

"I'm thinking, there seem to be a lot of posters of the Heaven’s Arrival."

"Oh, you mean that? It's really disturbing to see."

He scanned the old posters plastered across the alley walls. This ideology rejected the world's way of existence, seeking salvation through nothingness and death. Even Feodor couldn't understand or resonate with this strange ideology. He simply saw it as the product of a group of people who couldn't face the reality of life, making up excuses to avoid it.

Of course, the sheer number of posters didn't mean that all the residents of the city were influenced by it. Even just a few people, a loud minority, could make much noise and trouble. Yet, the thought that this city already had a place for such voices filled her heart with regret.

"Such a beautiful view is ruined, and it's a shame for the clean walls. Since they're sticking it so close together, they should have given more thought to the layout."

"Huh? You mean that’s the only part you're uncomfortable with?"

"Could there be any other reasons?" She asked with a blank expression.

"…It's okay, forget it. Um. Let's not talk about that. How's the situation ahead?"

"No problem. No suspicious figures have appeared in the direction we're heading… By the way, maybe we're the ones that stand out the most?" As she spoke, Lakish turned around.

Of course, she wasn't wearing her simple military uniform. At Giggir’s arrangement, a local merchant had prepared a set of clothes for her to change into. Her attire was so unrecognizable, her look was as simple as that of a local teenager. Putting aside the fact that the residents of Lyell City were practically deserting, this outfit still blended in well within the vast city of Collinadiluche.

"You look great in this."

"Thank you, I'll take it as a compliment," she replied readily.

"As for your outfit, well, it suits you perfectly. It's almost unbelievable."

Hearing her say this, Feodor looked down at his own attire. He wore a black suit and a matching coat, a black hat, and even dark glasses. It was the kind of outfit that made you wonder, "How much do you like black?" To put it bluntly, he looked like a gangster's underling.

"Is that… a compliment?"

"No, I mean it. You look really good in this outfit… I kind of think you look like a rich young man who's just gotten into bad habits. So cute."

*What with that kind of a description?* "Are you complimenting me?"

"I'm complimenting you."

Lakish chuckled as she spoke, but he couldn't help but feel happy.

Feodor (though it had been a long time since he lost his home) was indeed the son of a wealthy family. And, while he wasn't exactly a new learner, he had certainly been involved in bad things. Therefore, this analogy wasn't particularly flattering.

"Say, Feodor, don't you have a slightly sinister look? I don't know if I should say you're the type who's actually quite innocent but is misunderstood because of your appearance, or if I should say you're actively promoting that misconception. So, you're well-suited to this easy-to-understand 'little badass' look."

"You're not complimenting me, are you?"

"I am complimenting you."

With that, Feodor wasn't exactly fed up with this meaningless conversation, but he turned to face forwards. They were almost at their destination. "Okay, hopefully we can sneak in without any problems."

"To get in, why not just ring the bell at the main entrance?"

"Because he's not here. According to the subject—Dr. Margomedari Brompton—his usual schedule, he won't be back from work until late at night."

Indeed, he had deliberately chosen this time to arrive before sunset. It would have been a real hassle if the target was home.

"After all, I'm here to request long-term assistance from the target. I don't want to go to the target empty-handed like I am now."

"You're looking for something to threaten him with?"

"I don't deny it, but that's not entirely true."

Feodor stopped at the alley's exit.

He pressed his back against the wall, peering ahead. No residents were visible.

It wasn't just their attire; they were undoubtedly quite conspicuous here. He wanted to avoid being seen as much as possible. "When commissioning work from outside experts, you must have a basic understanding of what you intend to entrust them with, how they will interpret the commission, and what kind of work you actually want them to do. This is a commander's ironclad rule."

"…What?"

"Especially in this case, we may not be able to establish a friendly relationship. They may appear willing to help, but secretly plot betrayal. To see through this, we must have a minimal grasp of the implications of their every gesture. Furthermore, to prevent this from happening, we must prevent them from seeing what we know and how much we know. In other words, it's necessary to conceal some bargaining chips."

"…That's too difficult. I don't understand." Lakish tilted her head. "In other words, you're trying to create a mysterious situation before recruiting them, pretending to be a shrewd and capable boss?"

"Uh…yes, yes, that's right." Feodor nodded vaguely.

She seemed to be roughly correct. However, it felt as if some subtle nuance of meaning had been overlooked, or rather, it didn't quite ring true, leaving him feeling a bit disappointed.

 

The neighbourhoods in this area are enormous.

This statement wasn't an exaggeration; it was simply a statement of fact. In the area where Feodor and his companions were currently walking, almost every component of the neighbourhood was larger than elsewhere. From the buildings, window frames, doors, streetlights, paving stones, iron fences, and even the trash cans along the roadside. The only exceptions were things like street trees, perhaps only because they weren't quite as comically large.

"What a huge neighbourhood\!" Lakish murmured, reflecting on the neighbourhood. "It feels incredible, like stepping into a fairy tale."

"Coming from a fairy, that statement is even more convincing."

This area was specifically designed to accommodate the various races of Titanic size.

The city of Collinadiluche is home to a diverse range of races, so the neighbourhoods had to be designed with these different races in mind. The cultural clash alone is a difficult issue to overcome. No matter how laws are amended or how mutual understanding is fostered, integrating "different beings" will always be difficult. This is especially true of the issues arising from size differences, which are fundamentally unsolvable. A full-grown Titanic could not, even if he bent down desperately, fit into the home of a Gnome.

Thus, physical divisions are made based on the races…or rather, based on their general size and living preferences. Winged races live in well-ventilated, elevated areas; fish-like races live on the shores or bottoms of artificial lakes; shorter races live in areas where everything is smaller; taller races, on the other hand, gather in residential areas where everything is larger.

The latter residential area is where Feodor and his companions are now. 

"We've been tricked." Feodor sighed as he entered the house.

The room was in a state of disarray. Everything on the bookcase was scattered on the floor, the table was in an odd position, the carpet had been ripped apart, and the entire wardrobe, along with its contents, was overturned.

"Does this mean someone's been here before?"

This house was built within the residential area of ​​a Titanic race, and of course, its size rivalled that of the streetscape. The ceilings were high, the walls were far apart, the chairs were so high that you had to climb to sit on them, and the table was even higher than Feodor's eyes. He couldn't help but feel nostalgic. Perhaps this was the world he had seen as a child.

"It's really outrageous\! It's so messy\! It's going to take a lot of effort to clean it up."

Lakish quickly surveyed the surroundings.

After traversing the room—even the corridor was so wide and long that it would take ages to walk at a normal pace—Feodor shook his head.

"Every room is in the same condition." Feodor pondered for a moment.

"Are there any rooms intact? How's the mess?"

"Every room I've seen has been ransacked, but it doesn't look like they're rummaging through anything valuable."

"Are there any signs of resistance from the owner?"

"Absolutely not."

"What should I do? Should I go back?"

"No."

Feodor shook his head, then put on his thin gloves again and tried to pick up a book that had fallen to the floor…

But the book was too large and heavy, so he gave up. He left it lying on the floor and flipped through it quickly. It was a recipe for simple home-cooked meals, a complete collection of whole lamb dishes.

"Is this book special?"

"No, just a regular book."

He checked another book and found it was a collection of ancient fairytales. He immediately flipped to the next one, which featured a shop offering delicious cask wine. He flipped through the pages of the next book, then clutched the hardcover novel (which was unusually heavy due to its size) and said, "So it is."

After figuring it out, he turned and picked up the shattered remains of the clock from the thick carpet. After peering inside from various angles, his suspicions were confirmed.

"But then, if that's the case, what's going on… This is really troubling. I didn't expect it to be this bad." At that moment, his shirt was tugged.

"…Wait, stop pretending to have figured it out. Explain to me, what do you know?"

He hesitated. The information and speculations he had gathered so far hadn't yet formed a complete picture; only the outlines of the whole were vague.

Still, since she had asked, he owed her an answer. "First, the people who arrived earlier weren't looking to intimidate or for money, that goes without saying. Second, they weren't just one person, but a group of five to ten, possibly members of a fairly established criminal organization. Furthermore, their size wasn't like the Titanics who live in or near this house; they were about the same size as us.”

The object they were looking for was probably about the size of a piece of paper, something simple and obvious, and there's a high chance they've already found it. Or perhaps a competing, hostile organization has it and they don't want to clash with them."

Lakish nodded in response, listening, but… "…How do you know that?"

She posed a seemingly reasonable question.

This was, of course, a long story. Feodor, wanting to explain it briefly, thought for a moment. "As for the number of people, it's because their methods of searching the house vary. Some have been trained in searching homes, while others haven't. However, all of them tried to minimise noise while destroying things. Look, even though the house is completely destroyed, there aren't any scratches on the floor or walls, and the debris is thrown onto the carpet, which makes almost no sound. So, I can infer that, despite the varying levels of training, there's a certain order in the group. As for their size, it's simply because they threw things within reach. If a Titanic were to rummage through things, the area affected would likely be much larger. And then there's…" His gaze fell on the books scattered on the floor at his feet. "These books vary widely in type, and while their contents clearly don't match, they all show signs of having been roughly examined. Some of the thicker books have even been cut and read. This means the mysterious group's target is something that can be found between the pages. The way they investigated other locations suggests a similar conclusion, like the carpet being lifted up and the clock being damaged enough to clearly reveal the hollow interior."

He left his explanation at that for now.

"To put it simply, it's something like this. Do you understand—"

He noticed something.

He had unknowingly become too enthusiastic.

He kept his thoughts flowing, uninterrupted, as he sorted through the tangled mess in his mind. He usually tried to restrain himself, as it would be unbearable for anyone listening. However, once the mood struck, he couldn't help himself.

Isn't she dumbfounded?

Feodor turned to look at Lakish with trepidation.

"—Huh?"

How could he interpret the expression on her face? He could see the surprise and confusion, which was pretty much what he'd expected. But beyond that, he could see…

"You're truly worthy of me."

"Huh?"

Should I say trust? But how could that be?

"You're fully qualified to claim to be skilled in scheming. Your observation, analysis, and insight are far superior to my wildest dreams."

"Huh? Really?"

Her reaction was beyond his expectations.

He felt that this kind of self-absorbed, incessant chatter didn't leave a good impression.

For example, Tiat would frown and say, "Disgusting\!"; Panival would say, "That's very much your style," followed by a faint smile; Collon would say, "Sorry, I wasn't listening," followed by a laugh; and the old Lakish would say, "No, no, no, sorry. I don't understand, but I think it's amazing," where even though she was speaking up for him, she wouldn’t really be helping him at all—

"And what's next? You haven't finished yet, have you? Didn't you just say they might have found what they were looking for, or maybe they're avoiding a conflict with a rival organization?"

"Oh."

He regained his composure and reiterated the thought that had been stagnating in his mind.

"That part is easy, since no one's here. There are two possible scenarios: one is that they successfully achieved their goal and left, and the other is that they were thwarted and fled. I think the correct answer is probably the former. If it's the latter, those that 'thwarted' might be…"

He stopped mid-sentence.

"—Those guys?"

Lakish asked.

"Indeed. Really, I don't know if this timing is coincidental or unfortunate."

He looked up at the insanely high ceiling, then leaned against the wall and peered through the gap in the curtains. He could see suspicious figures moving between the hidden areas. "Ten people… No, probably more. They haven't launched an attack yet."

"If you count the ones who went around to the back, there are sixteen in total. They must be planning to surround this house. Their formation is very similar to the Winged Guard’s street warfare tactics. They probably anticipated a large number of thieves in this house and launched their operation on that assumption."

"A large number?" Lakish’s ears twitched. "There are only two of us."

"Yes."

So, that's what happened.

Now those people outside are mistaking them for the two of us who just happened to be there for the group that was rummaging through the house.

How unfortunate. They both sighed.

"If we communicate properly, can we resolve the misunderstanding? Just say we were just passing through."

"That's a great idea. We'll definitely try it when the world is filled with love and peace."

In other words, this idea will never be adopted. "So, should we fight? Three minutes should be enough to annihilate them." Despite being unarmed, Lakish flexed her shoulders.

Seniolis was large and heavy, and she hadn't brought it here. Therefore, Lakish’s current combat power was comparatively limited; but given the circumstances, her words weren't false, optimistic, or boastful. Once an adult Leprechaun unleashed its full magical power, a group of sixteen professionals wouldn't pose any threat. That was a fact.

However…

"We can't do that. They're probably the Winged Guard."

Feodor, peering through the gap in the curtains, stopped Lakish. "If you use Venenum, both your and my identities will be completely exposed. I don't want my intentions to be discovered before we can even begin our plan."

"You mean, you want me to kill everyone, right?"

"I preferred the gentle, life-respecting version of you\!"

Lakish replied, "Just kidding," but it was unclear how much truth that held. "In that case, we'll have to break through using conventional methods. Can you keep up with me?"

"Of course."

The two of them faced the window, exchanging a glance to show their understanding.

Then they pulled their hats down and covered their mouths with scarves, more or less obscuring their faces.

"By the way, that Dr. Margomedari is quite popular."

"That said, I guess we need to think a little more about how to approach him."

They joked, calculating their timing.

"One, two…"

Lakish stared out the window, counting. Feodor, observing her profile, suddenly thought of Tiat. *I wonder where that idiot is and what she's doing now.* *Is she alone again, perched atop the abandoned theatre on Floating Island 38, staring into the distant sky?*

The delicious bakeries are mostly closed, and Lakish, the skilled cook, is no longer around. No one will make her delicious donuts anymore. So, she probably hasn't eaten anything, hasn't spoken to anyone, and just sits there.

Just like when they first met.

"Three\!"

His recollection lasted only a moment; real time passed mercilessly.

The window flung open, and Feodor and Lakish leaped onto the street.

### **Part 5 – Two People in the Dark**

Speaking of which, there's a man here.

His name is Margomedari Brompton.

He calls himself a "great sinner."

Regul Aire is inhabited by a diverse array of races. Almost all races don't just form fixed tribes with their own kind—despite the various challenges and problems they face, they all live together in mixed communities, forming villages and cities.

However, some races, though only a few, find it difficult to coexist with others.

The soil-dwelling Myrmex and the aquatic fish-headed people are obvious examples. For example, the Cygne, the winged race who lived on mountaintops and self-styled ruling class, use culture and tradition as excuses to resist interaction with other races. These races can only live in their own neighbourhoods.

This tavern is located on the edge of one of those "race-specific neighbourhoods."

The sun had long since set, and closing time was approaching. While the place wasn't always busy, it was natural that the customers would be even fewer at this time of year. Only one regular, a male customer, sat at the corner of the bar, quietly sipping from his glass.

With a soft click, the door opened. The owner, wiping glasses, looked up at the new customer.

"Excuse me, it's almost closing time—"

"Finally found it."

It was a woman's voice.

The male regular slowly raised his head and looked toward the door. Standing there was a tiny woman whose appearance and voice could match the strength of his.

The man's face, previously radiating the look of an exhausted old man, slowly took on a touch of surprise.

"…Why are you here?"

The woman lowered her eyes and shook her head slightly.

"I have a favour to ask of you."

"No."

He refused with a single word.

"I haven't said anything yet."

"I know you well, even if you don't say it. I know you—at least I know what you, young lady, would want right now."

"In that case…"

"That's exactly why\!"

He interrupted the woman again, his tone brimming with determination, unwilling to let her finish. "That's why I said no. Not only is that dangerous and unacceptable, but it's also nearly impossible."

"But…"

"No buts. Let's leave it at that. No need to discuss this further."

There was a brief silence.

"At this point, I no longer have the right to cherish myself."

"That's your excuse. Everyone has the right to cherish their own life; it can't be taken away by anyone." The man calmly interrupted, while the woman continued unmoved.

"Having come this far, I don't intend to seek anyone's forgiveness. No, if I stop here, even I won't be able to forgive myself."

"You could be a little more tolerant of yourself, just as those around you accept and forgive you."

"That's the only thing I don't want to hear from you." The woman shook her head impatiently. "The so-called near-impossibility is actually good news to me. After all, you chose not to leave the term 'impossible' by itself."

Alas. The man stared at the ceiling with despair. Oh, this is truly unbelievable. This girl, this noble lady, her love is truly too deep. She knows full well that excessive love can burn oneself, yet she resolutely sets out towards that end.

"You…"

After a moment's hesitation, he decided to speak to stop her, but before he could even begin, he swallowed his words back.

He could hear approaching footsteps from behind the woman, further down the alley. There weren't just one or two people, but more than ten, each walking at a different pace, quickly approaching.

The woman turned—but the footsteps were already a step ahead of her, emerging from the other side of the darkness. They wore matching dark grey coats and carried long-barrelled gunpowder rifles. All of them walked silently through the doorway and into the shop.

"What are you doing?" The woman raised her voice, a mixture of confusion and anger. However, the intruders ignored her and surrounded the man sitting in the corner of the bar.

"Are you Dr. Margomedari Brompton?" one of the short Reptraces asked in a raspy voice.

"This place is closing soon. If you want to have a drink together, you should find another place."

"Are you Dr. Margomedari Brompton?" the Reptrace asked again, completely ignoring the man's joke.

Eleven men quietly raised their muskets, each pointed at the man.

"…Alas, I'm not a well-known figure, and I don't recall handing out business cards to people like you."

The Titanic man gave a wry, almost tired, smile. The intruders, perhaps interpreting his response as an admission of confidence, nodded to each other, then adjusted their stance and surrounded the man more tightly.

The muzzles of their guns pressed against his back. The woman gasped.

"Please come with us."

"Refusing… is useless, right?" The man gulped down the liquid in his glass and stood up from the stool, as if in resignation.

He began to move slowly, as if he had difficulty walking.

He stopped at the door. The woman stood there, her head slightly lowered.

"…Senior, where are you going?"

"Anywhere else? At least not to drag you and this shop down with me."

"These people…" She paused. "What are the Winged Guard planning to do next?"

"I can't tell you that. You understand, right? You should understand." Another gun prodded the huge man's buttocks, and he weakly acknowledged it.

"—I don't want to."

The man suddenly realized something and looked up. He stared intently at the woman, whose shoulders were shaking slightly.

"No, you can't do that\! Give it up\!" He said.

He frantically tried to stop her.

A look of confusion crossed the intruders’ faces, puzzled by his actions.

"You still have time. The future is still limitless. But if you do that, even you will end up on our side. This is a road of no return, a road of no return\!"

One gun pointed at the woman.

The others hesitated for a moment, then aimed at the woman as well.

The woman slowly raised her drooping face.

"…So, what you're saying is, as long as I reach the point of no return, you'll be willing to listen to me, senior, and won't turn a deaf ear to me—"

"No\!"

The man's shouts were no longer audible to the woman. "You… you alone cannot stand against these guys\!"

### **Part 6 – The First Division of the Winged Guard**

Dr. Margomedari Brompton.

Cyclops, physician, and researcher. Medicine, linguistics, astronomy, physics, engineering, history, business administration, mysticism… He had repeatedly attended and graduated from academic academies over the decades, a distinguished talent with expertise in a wide range of fields. The Cyclopes were a remarkably long-lived race, and it was not uncommon for them to devote their long lives to scholarship. However, few dabbled in such diverse fields as he did without restraint.

He was, for the most part, affiliated with the General Medical Clinic in Collinadiluche city, responsible for directing the development of various pharmaceuticals and treatments. He had also been the project leader for decades studying the ecology and adulthood tuning techniques of Leprechauns. Furthermore, due to professional needs, he had once been appointed a Second Enchanted Weapons Technician, though that was decades ago.

In other words, he was the Cyclops physician who had tuned all current adult fairy soldiers.

"Oh\! Oh\! It's him\! That burly old man\!"

Noft nodded repeatedly. Of course, Tiat remembered this person. He was a giant with one eye, dressed in a white suit resembling an oversized bedsheet. During the pre-tuning consultation, she had been so tiny in comparison that he had to arch his back like a cat just to meet her eyes. This had left a lasting impression on her.

"So… that's his name…" Tiat muttered. Now, she realized once again the unspoken truth that everyone has a name.

"He was also a senior who was strongly respected by Naigrat during her school days. I wonder how many times that happened to Dr. Margomedari."

"Oh?"

After hearing this, they still didn't understand.

"So? Is that old man the next target of assassination?"

"That's right."

A brief silence followed.

"How could that be possible?"

Tiat agreed. She nodded silently.

The Cyclopes were enormous, and possessed a weight commensurate with their size. Furthermore, the vitality inherent in them is powerful enough to rival that of Ogres. Ordinary blades can't penetrate their skin, and poisons have never been reported to be effective against them. Even if struck by a gunpowder gun, it likely wouldn't cause much damage. Leaving aside the truly immortal Beasts, they're probably among the most difficult creatures to kill in all Regul Aire.

"Well, who knows? If they're willing to give up because they think, 'How could that be possible?' then things would be much simpler."

Walking down the street, a few memories gradually resurfaced in Tiat's mind.

The first time she walked this street, it was with Willem. She'd said many impulsive things, and while he seemed dumbfounded by his inability to control her, he still seemed to happily comply with her wilful demands.

The second time they came here, they all came together. Lakish was there, too. Although she seemed quiet at the time, she was even more excited than Tiat's first visit. Tiat was dragged around, tossed around, and made a mess, but it was a very happy memory.

—Ah, why?

She had been watching this place through the Image Crystal since she was a child. She had memorised every detail of which movie series had been filmed on which street. However, the memories she recalled while walking along the street weren't the plots she had seen through the crystal, but memories of herself and the others running around in this place.

The group passed through the main gate of the Winged Guard headquarters.

"…Hmm?"

A subtle atmosphere permeated the air. It wasn't the tense atmosphere of a so-called warzone. No one was shouting, no one was running around. Instead, the soldiers coming and going exuded a strange, trembling tension.

"I rarely come here," Tiat said, looking around. "But, the atmosphere here? It seems to have changed quite a bit…"

"After all, it's the First Division using this place now. It's certainly different from when Limeskin’s Second Division was here."

Even within the Winged Guard, the First Division's purpose is said to be to mediate excessive conflicts between floating islands. Therefore, they don't target immortal enemies like the Beasts; they only fight against the living, the inhabitants of Regul Aire.

This is a far cry from the feeling they had when facing the Beasts. Perhaps that's why this place is filled with an uncomfortable tension, Tiat thought.

"But it doesn't feel just like that. I hope something troublesome hasn't happened again—"

"Third Engineering Officer Grick Graycrack?”

The short, sheep-headed private spoke to them. "Are the other two you're with, Private Noft Kei Oracion and Tiat Shiba Ignareo?"

"Yes, that's right. Did you receive the message? The Second and Fifth Divisions are sending reinforcements regarding the 'Blackened Dagger' incident."

Blackened Dagger. This seems to be a codeword for the serial assassinations that caused the commotion. The reason for the codeword is probably because they can't use the term "serial killings" everywhere, but it doesn't make any difference.

"Yes, yes, I did hear about it, but…?"

"We've just finished a long journey, and let everyone rest… I'd like to say that, but it looks like something has already happened. Could you please give us a rough outline of the situation? Or could you take us to someone who has the authority to tell us about this?"

"No, uh, well…"

The private just kept mumbling, and the conversation didn't seem to progress. "Hey, you, is what I'm saying so hard to understand?"

"No, no, no, I don't mean to. By the way, if you need a break, well, I can arrange it for you three right away. I'll take you to the officers' room…"

"No, I want you to tell me what happened first."

The private, pressed again, seemed to finally give in.

"…I'm sorry, but according to orders from the First Division's commander-in-chief, I can't share any information with you." He lowered his head and said this.

"Huh?"

"What?"

It was Noft who was frantically speaking.

"What's going on now? Why did things turn out like this?"

"I'm so sorry you all came all the way here, but I really can't let you get involved in this…"

Noft’s cheek twitched. "What the hell\!"

It was as if a blood vessel burst.

Noft stalked recklessly down the corridor.

"Wait… wait a minute, senior. Calm down." Tiat hurried after her.

"I'm perfectly calm\!"

"No one who says that is truly calm\! Oh, come on, Mr. Glick, please help her\! Why are you laughing?"

"Ah, no, it's not that I'm not angry, it's just that she got angry first, and I missed the opportunity. Her anger is much milder now, so it's okay for you, little girl, to hold her back."

"That's irresponsible\!"

Tiat grabbed Noft's waist, hoping to hold her back, but it was no use. Noft’s forceful advance dragged her away, leaving her crawling along the corridor. Luckily, no one else was passing by; she didn't want anyone but other fairies to see her.

"Hey, I'm coming in\!"

Of course, Noft wouldn't just knock. She forcefully opened the door to the First Division's headquarters, as if to force her way in.

"…What a racket." The person she was looking for was indeed inside. The giant with the black goat head, who had been standing by the window gazing out, slowly turned his head.

"You are the commander-in-chief here?"

Senior—\! Tiat tried to shout, but the sound didn’t make it out.

"Indeed, I am a First Officer of Collinadiluche, appointed commander-in-chief of the First Division of the Winged Guard. So, who are you, the rude person asking this question?" His voice was steady and imbued with authority.

"I am Noft Kei Oracion, a high-ranking soldier of the Second Division. Commander-in-Chief, I'm sure you understand the significance of stating that name."

"…Oh, you're that fairy weapon?" The black goat-headed man looked completely uninterested. "This is the first time I've seen it in person. So, the rumours about being able to speak like a person are true."

"──────Oh?"

"Senior\! Wait, stop, give up\! You can't do that. If you keep being rude, it'll get Mr. Limeskin and the others in trouble\!"

I'm a little like Lakish now… Tiat thought as she desperately lunged at Noft. Everyone around her was making a scene, and she desperately tried to stop them, but no one listened.

How should I put it? Doing this kind of thing is more physically and mentally draining than I thought. Has Lakish always felt this way? The next time I see her, I'll be sure to thank her for her hard work and apologise.

Grick suddenly poked his head through the crack of the open door. "Okay, okay, I'm sorry for all the noise. I'm Grick Graycrack, a Third Engineering Officer with the Second Division. I have something to ask you."

"You're the overseer of this weapon, huh? Once the reins are handed to you, you're responsible for keeping them. You don't seem like a diligent person."

"Oh?" Grick chuckled. "You're quite discerning. I personally still can't figure out why I ended up wearing such a cramped uniform."

"I suppose so. Lime always likes to recruit lost souls like you. I've known him for years, but his philosophical bent is something I never understand, no matter how much time passes." The goat-head shook his head wearily.

Huh? Tiat was puzzled. His words and actions just now seemed to express dissatisfaction, but for some reason, she couldn't sense any ill will or hostility from the man before her toward Lime— First Officer Limeskin. If I had to say it, it was more like respect or admiration…

"Regardless, even if they're unneeded reinforcements, they're still guests. I don't mean to leave you out."

"How dare you say that\!" Noft interjected.

"Please, senior, calm down\!"

The Goat-Head ignored the two fairies tangling together and said to Grick:

"Let me confirm the reason for your uninvited visit. It's because you're unhappy about being excluded from the 'Blackened Dagger' event, correct?"

"I'm glad you understood so quickly." Grick shrugged. "We're here to help out. If we just find the situation a little awkward, that's fine, but to be kicked out without even a reason is unbearable."

"So, all I need to do is tell you the reason."

The goat-head sighed, a breath that sounded neither like a sigh nor a mockery. "Dr. Margomedari Brompton was kidnapped last night."

"…Huh?"

"That's confirmed. You can check it out if you want."

"Ah, no… I don't doubt it."

Noft let out a sound of admiration. "They kidnapped that old man…I don't know who he is, but he's pretty tough."

Indeed. While the statement was imprudent, that aside, Noft's words made sense.

After all, the kidnappee was a Cyclops. Just being a Cyclops meant something, whether they were scholars or not. They were tall, strong, and incredibly powerful. Whether it was knocking them unconscious, forcing them into submission at gunpoint, or drugging them and secretly moving them away, all the conventional tactics used in "kidnapping" seemed useless.

What methods had the perpetrators used? "Undercover soldiers from the Noble Wings Empire have been lingering in this city lately. While they're suspected of being behind the attack, it's unlikely. They're an independent force, separate from the Empire, and they're currently on the run with their target, Margomedari."

Tiat had a bad feeling. "Um," she raised a hand amidst a tangle with Noft. "I apologise for interrupting you two. I'm First-class Equivalent Soldier Tiat Shiba Ignareo of the Fifth Division. May I ask a question?"

The goat-headed man snorted. "You'll be allowed to ask, fairy weapon."

"Thank you. Uh… could that criminal be silver-haired and Markless? His eyes are fierce, and while his demeanour is friendly, he gives off an air of disbelief.”

Although she found it unlikely, she couldn't rule it out. The timing was perfect, coinciding with the guy's (presumably) arrival on the floating island. Furthermore, the presence of a third force of unknown origin compelled her to doubt it.

"No." The goat-headed man answered quickly. "The criminal's identity has been determined. They’re characteristically Markless, but other than that, they don’t fit the profile Ignareo outlined."

Ah, what? So that's how it is. She breathed a sigh of relief. At the same time, she felt a touch of regret. If that guy were the culprit, she could pursue him openly and bring him back with her head held high.

"So? How does this relate to the reasoning behind excluding us?"

"Don't worry, I'm not finished yet… I wanted to, but I've almost said everything I wanted to say. There's one more thing you should know, and that's the name of the criminal I mentioned earlier."

"Can you please stop beating around the bush? I'm not very patient." Noft, impatient as ever.

"Naigrat Astartus.”

The goat-headed man simply stated the criminal's name.

"…Huh?"

Everyone present murmured in confusion.

"Ah, that's not right. Only underage Trolls use their father's name as their surname. Forget that name." The goat-headed man calmly corrected the name slightly before resuming his speech.

"The criminal's name is Naigrat. This is why I can't let you participate in the investigation. While our work can involve so-called close relationships, it's not so cruel as to ask you to help arrest family." 

## **Chapter 3 – “A Conversation with the Voiceless, or…” / “Crossing Road”**

### **Part 1 – The Fugitive**

Speaking of which, there's a woman named Naigrat here.

She's a Troll, and her age… well, over twenty. Hmm.

As a young girl, she attended the Central Comprehensive Academy for about five years, earning four qualifications, including one in basic medicine. Upon graduation, she immediately used these certificates to work for the Orlandri Trading Company, one of the largest trade associations in Regul Aire. Her life goal at the time was "a smooth, elite life," and she was quite successful halfway through.

But halfway through, she fell completely.

The reason wasn't a big deal; there were things she couldn't bear, things she couldn't ignore, children she couldn't leave behind, and places she couldn't abandon. As she turned to face these things, she unknowingly ended up in her current state.

In fact, she didn't really care about the incident itself. She didn't regret her choice, and it had led her to her current job, which she considered her life’s calling. If she were told she could return to the elite life she'd always dreamed of, she would still refuse without hesitation.

So, naturally—even now, being hunted by an unknown armed group, she felt no regrets.

"Oh, this is unbearable\! They're so persistent\!"

She ran through an alley still slick with rainwater.

Compared to the homes of other races, everything in the settlements of the Titanic races was massive. Even Naigrat, not small for a Markless, felt as if she were viewing the world through the eyes of a child, a truly fascinating sight.

*(Is this what it's like to see the streets from Almita's height…?)*

Even though she knew now wasn't the time to dwell on such things, she couldn't help but think about them. If this weren't the case, she would have loved to savour this feeling a little longer. "Little Nai, that's a dead end\!"

Following her closely was a one-eyed being whose size perfectly matched the scenery. It was Margomedari Brompton, Naigrat’s senior at the Academy, and a physician who had received much support from her at work, and now, a companion in their escape, sharing life and death.

"Really, senior, didn't I tell you not to call me Little Nai? I'm not a child anymore."

She ran without stopping, only turning her head.

In the night, illuminated by the streetlights, she couldn't see the pursuers directly, but the footsteps and voices were approaching. If she turned back now, she would probably run into them before she could even get to the next street. "You could give up, but you're so diligent\!", she muttered. 

"Nonsense\! If they were lazy, the Regul Aire would have collapsed long ago\!"

"In that case, why don't we just run away? How about we just eat them all… Ah, no, we can't finish that much. It would be against etiquette if we don't finish all the prepared food right away."

"I'm glad you've started to give up on this ridiculous escape\! But if possible, I hope you'll also consider the law and morality\!"

As they talked, the situation gradually worsened.

The monocular being’s massive body wasn't suited to this kind of escape scenario. After all, hiding behind cover or stealthy footsteps were practically impossible. In other words, the only way to escape was to run and put more distance between them.

"Ah."

In the direction they were heading, about five men, each dressed in a different way, rushed out one after another. Judging from their attire, they all looked like travellers, a common sight in the city of Collinadiluche. But their movements were uniformly trained, and they were wielding oversized gunpowder rifles, their expressions far from polite and friendly. Very much unlike the average traveller on the street.

*(…Have we been outflanked?)*

Naigrat paused, instinctively looking back.

Of course, the pursuers were still chasing them. Within sight, there were seven of them. They were rapidly climbing the slope, gradually approaching, each armed with another type of oversized gunpowder rifle.

A gunpowder rifle, as its name suggests, is a portable weapon that fires a bullet by detonating gunpowder. One of the characteristics of this weapon is the close correlation between size and power. In other words, the larger the gunpowder rifle, the greater its lethality. Even a gunpowder rifle that could be used with one hand could be fully effective for assassination purposes. The fact that they had brought out a larger gunpowder rifle meant they were already anticipating a proper firefight.

Ogres are, at least slightly, stronger than most of the other Markless races. Gunfire of this magnitude wouldn't seriously injure them, and their wounds heal quickly. The Cyclopes were equally strong, so they didn't seem to need to worry about any damage from such weaponry—that's what Naigrat thought. Of course, if they were hit, it would still hurt a bit.

The group in front, dressed as travellers, and the group in military uniforms behind them noticed each other.

They both stopped without a word, keeping their distance and raising their guns, clearly on guard against each other.

"Oh…"

She had thought she was being ambushed or pincered, but that didn't seem to be the case.

Did these two different factions stumble upon each other at an unexpected place and time?

"…Who are you?" she asked the group dressed as travellers, but no one answered.

"Those guys over there are the Winged Guard, right?" she asked the group in military uniforms, but again, no one answered. "Hmm."

She could certainly consider forcing her way through one side's formation. Although Naigrat was merely an ordinary woman (as she called herself), she wasn't incompetent in combat. The Ogres possessed ridiculous strength and vitality. Even without training or exercise, they could easily crush a mere ten or so armed soldiers.

However, this wouldn't break the deadlock. Furthermore, the two forces were already holding each other in check, and if the balance was disrupted, she wasn't sure what the consequences would be. Moreover, regardless of which side was pursuing them, their reserve forces were likely to be larger than the number they saw. The longer they dragged on, the more their opponents would recruit more troops and employ more sophisticated tactics to corner them, making it increasingly difficult for them to escape. They might even run out of energy in such a situation. If Naigrat were alone, she'd be confident she could handle a longer, more drawn-out battle like this one. However, the Cyclops accompanying her, despite his massive size, possessed a gentle and delicate heart. Putting aside the physical injuries, the sheer intensity of the fighting and the harm he suffered would likely be too much for him to handle.

Naigrat concluded there was no escape route and looked left and right.

However, they were on a bridge with high piers. No matter which way she looked, all she could see were low iron railings and the traces of a large, dried-up canal stretching far below.

"Naigrat\!”

One of the men in military uniforms called out to her from a distance.

"Huh? You're calling me?"

The other party had somehow discovered her details. "You're currently kidnapping a high-ranking official and suspected of assassinating multiple others\! I urge you to surrender immediately and release the professor\!"

"Kidnapping… me? Huh? Me?"

For a moment, she was confused by the accusation.

"What are you talking about? You're mistaken\! You were the ones who tried to take senior away by force\! You even pulled out those terrifying guns\!"

She protested, but the other party wasn't kind enough to answer her questions.

Although this wasn't meant to be a response, everyone crept forward, gradually closing the distance.

"Besides, why are the Winged Guard chasing senior? Protecting Regul Aire is your job, right? If so, you should be capturing more dangerous individuals\!"

Everyone present—even Margomedari Brompton behind her—said nothing. Naigrat, enraged by this, raised her voice even higher. "You guys over there, too\! What do you want from my senior? Let me be frank, he's not rich\! He gets a generous salary, but he spends it all on academic books or paying for re-enrolment at the academy\!"

"Stop it, little girl. I'm embarrassed." Margomedari lowered his head bashfully and tugged at her sleeve. "Just let me go. No, this is the best decision."

"Let's talk about that later."

"I'm serious. If I'm captured, this situation will end smoothly, and your suspicion will be cleared as well. Then…"

"And then there's my business." She interrupted Margomedari’s rapid speech. "I haven't told you about my situation yet, senior. I didn't come all the way to Floating Island 11 just to play hide-and-seek. There's one thing I absolutely must ask of you—"

"I can't do it. I can’t promise."

"—I haven't said anything yet."

"I know that without even hearing it, so I'm saying it's impossible. Tuning fairies is far more dangerous than you think. No, you should have noticed even this little bit, right?"

Of course I had. Naigrat swallowed the words back.

Leprechauns are born throughout the floating islands. Those that grow to a certain degree are taken under the care of the Winged Guard and transported to the Fairy Warehouse on Floating Island 68\. They are raised there, and when they reach adulthood, they are transported back to Floating Island 11 for tuning to adulthood, or rather to survive it. After that, they are supposed to be taken back by their respective military divisions for management and operation, but traditionally, they return to Floating Island 68 and are managed alongside the other young fairies when not on missions.

There are several suspicious aspects to this system. For one, the fairies' tuning is limited to Floating Island 11, in the city of Collinadiluche.

Generally speaking, adjustments closer to Floating Island 68 would be more efficient. Even if specialised facilities are necessary, they could simply be built near Island 68 or relocated there; even moving the Fairy Warehouse to Island 11 would be preferable. No, if they truly fear for the future of the Regul Aire, they should do so. After all, they are the Leprechauns who bear the weight of everyone’s fate.

Naigrat had received a brief explanation of the reason for this decision, and she understood it. The fairy weapon system itself was a source of conflict within the Winged Guard and the Orlandri Trading Company, making it impossible to always adopt strictly logical measures. She understood the reasoning, and after understanding it, she also sensed that there might be hidden secrets in this matter. Despite having sensed something, despite knowing something…

"So, Little Nai—"

"Senior, you don't understand at all."

She had known about that for a long time. Having sensed something, knowing something, that's why she came here.

"You don't understand a thing\!"

She suddenly grabbed the Cyclops by the collar.

Then, she lifted him up, as if plucked from the ground.

He was suspended high in the air.

In terms of weight alone, the Cyclops weighed about as much as a small carriage. Even the strongest Ogre would still feel some strain. But she couldn't complain about this small difficulty. The person she was now had come here carrying something far greater.

"Wow, wait… wait a minute\!" He shouted frantically, and the soldiers and the figures dressed as travellers were equally panicked. What was this Ogre planning to do? No one present could react. "Little… Little Nai, put me down. I'm afraid of heights."

One of them spoke as if she had accurately predicted what was about to happen.

"Didn't I tell you not to call me Little Nai, senior?"

“Huh?\!”

She didn't yell out loud, but simply gathered her strength and hurled the weight.

Not forward, not backward, but sideways over the railing.

"I'm not a child anymore."

Uwaa…

She twitched her numb legs and patted the dazed Margomedari beside her.

"Alright, senior, let's go."

She grabbed his hand and dragged him along, breaking into another run.

Sporadic gunfire rang out from behind, but the next moment, a voice called out, "Stop it, you idiot\!" She couldn't tell if it came from the Winged Guard or the other mysterious group, but it was a good thing. While getting hit by bullets wouldn't hurt much, she hated having holes in her clothes when she went out.

This distance should be safe… After they reached what they considered a safe distance, they decided to rest in a hidden area.

"Why did it come to this?" Naigrat muttered, sitting on a wooden box.

"You still have the nerve to say that? You're the least qualified person to say that, aren't you, Little Nai?" Margomedari, leaning against a nearby brick wall, shook his head.

"I've already said it. Don't call me Little Nai."

"…Even if you say that, in my eyes, you're still a child. Even now. That's your actual age, and that's your carefree, reckless personality."

Cyclops are extremely long-lived, easily living for a hundred or two hundred years. Therefore, in their eyes, most other races appear very young. It's unavoidable, but…

"Even so, I'm here for the all-important children, so I can't be treated like a child any longer. I can't compromise on things I can't compromise on," she replied firmly.

Then came the next step. Naigrat took a moment to catch her breath and said, "Almita has fallen into a coma."

She unexpectedly cut to the chase. Almita is the oldest of the young Leprechauns currently in the Fairy Warehouse. She had a "dream" that signalled her transition to adulthood over a year ago, but she hasn't had the necessary tuning to become an adult fairy, and so things have deteriorated to where they are today.

"She spends almost the entire day just dreaming. The medicine we received is no longer effective. Eudea and Masha are fine right now, but they're slowly becoming more and more vulnerable."

"…That's the natural lifespan of fairies. Those children's lives will end before they reach adulthood. It's proof that they've lived their lives correctly, in their own way, and it's a natural progression." Hearing Margomedari’s words, it felt like he was convinced.

Naigrat pouted at the words.

"Regardless of the consequences, if there's a way to prolong life, even if we must violate the laws of nature, we must do it no matter what. That's the physician's mission. Didn't you used to say that, senior?"

"…I do think I did, and it does sound a lot like something I would say…"

"You said it yourself. You should take responsibility for this."

"Haha, I really shouldn't have lived this long. Otherwise, the shackles on you would only grow heavier." Margomedari jokingly said something discouraging, looking up at the sky—and then.

"…Did you hear that?"

"Yeah."

The sound was the hurried footsteps of over ten people. Though they were still far away, they would likely arrive here soon.

"Oh no\! Let's run."

She stood up, but the Cyclops beside her didn't move. "Yes, it's better if you escape, Naigrat. That way, at least all the children in the warehouse won't lose their mother, and they can avoid this worst of all—"

"Really? Why are you acting so down and wanting to give up? You should come with me, too. We haven't even finished talking yet\!"

"That won't work… I haven't seen you in a while, and I really want to talk to you more, but I'm not very familiar with the roads around here, and I'd be caught in a heartbeat if I tried to escape. So, why not just escape on your own?

“Odette Jessman."
