### **Part 2 – The Running Boy, The Chasing Girl**

"Should we just burn it all down? Don't worry, we'll erase all the evidence."

"Please don't."

This conversation repeated itself countless times.

Being hunted relentlessly.

Running desperately.

Even shot at (missed).

Finally, nearly cornered in a narrow alley, he was saved by an Orc merchant who had learned the whole story from Giggir.

†

 

Many people imagine Orc dwellings as dirty and crowded places.

However, this impression is largely misleading. The average Orc family is generally very tidy. Other Beastfolk, on the other hand, are prone to leaving their hair everywhere due to seasonal shedding, and can even be said to cause more dirt than Orcs. Some Beastfolk might object, "Don't those guys bathe in mud?" This is certainly true; it's Orc custom. Records also mention that in ancient times on the surface, they would soak their bodies in fertilizer and dirty water. However, in modern Regul Aire, that culture has been literally refined. Today, they fill their bathtubs with an amber-coloured liquid made from high-quality clay dissolved in expensive scented oils; it can no longer be called simply mud.

*(But, that's probably only for the wealthy…)*

After being led to the luxurious guest room, he paused for breath, pondering this.

This room's decor was no less impressive than the one where he had spoken with Giggir, with extravagant spending to the point of vulgarity. The gold artifacts scattered throughout the place reflected the light, making it quite dazzling.

"The old man said you're family, so you're already part of our community and neighbourhood," said the shop's owner, a Orc. Incidentally, he couldn't tell the difference between the owner and Giggir.

The Orcs are numerous and united (indeed, this is also due to their poor relations with other races), so they tend to establish communal communities within each floating island and city.

These neighbourhoods, also known as Orc districts, are like cities or even countries in and of themselves, making it difficult for outsiders to interfere.

"Don't feel uncomfortable just because you're a Markless race. Treat this place like home."

"Then I'll comply."

"Huh, why are you still so reserved?"

He pretended not to hear the strange laughter and sipped the tea offered.

"…If you wish, you can also give my daughter a child."

Puff\!

He and Lakish both spat out their tea.

The Orcs didn't practice pair marriages, which was logical given they’re a polygamous species. Males and females mate freely, bear children freely, and raise them collectively. Therefore, they sometimes made sudden proposals that other species would find ethically questionable.

In fact, he actually introduced his daughter to Feodor.

Although Feodor had emphatically rejected his proposal, Lakish looked at him with a somewhat cold gaze afterward.

"That girl has beautiful skin, doesn’t she?"

A slightly narrowed, disapproving look, accompanied by a voice like a sharp blade.

But, purely in a general sense, that smooth, pink skin was indeed beautiful.

"Isn't it a perfect match for you, who hates the Markless?"

No, wait. He did hate the Markless, but he couldn't recall ever saying anything other than Markless was therefore acceptable.

"Which is to say, even regardless of race, that girl is just your type?"

Oh, her mood just wouldn't lift. No, to tell the truth, he didn't even know why she was angry. Although Lakish was indeed very dependent on Feodor now, she probably didn't consider that feeling to be love. Earlier, when she pointed at Tiat, with whom she’d clashed, and said "She's your lover, isn't she?", she didn't show any anger or jealousy.

"Hmph."

*Sigh, what did she want from him?*

Unable to sit still, Feodor fled to the bathroom.

After using the restroom, he washed his hands. Alone, he could finally think about serious matters.

There were so many things he needed to think about in this situation.

Dr. Margomedari Brompton. He was not only a Cyclops doctor, but also one of the very few who knew the theory underpinning the tuning of fairies, and was perhaps the only one who knew the detailed procedures of the whole process.

*(Besides us, there are several other organizations pursuing him. If that were the only reason, it would be fine, but one of them seems to be the Winged Guard…)*

Where is the doctor, exactly? From the most simplistic perspective, he's probably being held by the Winged Guard. However, judging by the sheer number and toughness of the Winged Guard soldiers chasing him, something seems off.

Yes, if the Winged Guard is also lingering on the streets because of the doctor, their target, then if he has escaped everything starts to make sense. If that's the case, he can use what he just witnessed to determine the events that has led to that kind of development.

*(Roughly speaking, there are two possibilities. Either the doctor betrayed the Winged Guard, or the Winged Guard betrayed the doctor… No, that seems premature; there are too many uncertainties.)*

As he pondered this, he put away his handkerchief and walked a few steps into the hallway.

—This kind of thing occasionally happens in a house with such grand decor.

At the corner of the hallway, a large mirror hung on the wall.

"…Tsk."

Moments later, a headache washed over him.

Mirrors faithfully reproduce and reflect whatever is before them. Therefore, whether it's the white walls, the white carpet, or the dazzling crystal lamp, the scenery behind them is literally reflected, and the mirror can see the same things as in reality.

Only, there’s a single difference this time. On the other side of the mirror, there's no Feodor Jessman. There's a young man with black hair and black eyes, a species with no known origins.

That person is laughing.

Looking at that smile, it feels as if you can hear a "hahaha" laugh at any moment.

Feodor couldn't help but put his hand to his mouth to check. He wasn't laughing, only the person in the mirror was laughing.

"What's so funny?"

"Yes—funny—ah—"

Although it was intermittent, he thought he heard something.

But, of course, it was an auditory hallucination. Or perhaps it was the scattered echoes of Feodor's own words.

It was like talking to himself against a wall.

"Are you kidding me?"

"—Jokes—on me?"

"What the hell are you?"

"What the hell are you—"

"I can’t stand it. This is ridiculous."

Feodor, driven to despair, decided to answer his own questions.

"I am the enemy of the Leprechauns."

"I am the destroyer of Regul Aire."

Alas, it was true. A mirror is just a mirror, nothing more. Since there's no way to have a conversation, there's no point in doing this…

*—Huh?*

"Hey… Hey\!"

He noticed something was wrong and clutched at the mirror, but the black-haired young man was no longer on the other side.

Only a young man with silver hair and purple eyes, looking at him with a panicked expression, as if cornered.

What was that just now? What was that guy saying? What did that sentence mean? *"What are you doing?"* He was about to lose himself in thought as he stared into the mirror when someone spoke to him. At the other end of the hallway, Lakish opened the door a crack and poked her head out.

"It's okay… there's just something dirty stuck in my hair."

"Hmm."

I don't know if Lakish believed it or if she didn't care, but she hummed and waved softly.

"Come back after you’ve finished with the restroom. I heard they've gathered intelligence."

They mobilised the Orcs living in the area to track the movements of those running around the streets. They demonstrated exceptional abilities in these types of group operations, where teamwork is crucial. They immediately transmitted back accurate and extensive intelligence.

"Have you got the map ready?"

"Here."

They spread out a map of the neighbourhood on the table and, like chess pieces, meticulously analysed the reports.

Information captured at a single moment wasn't of much value. However, gathering all this information, he could vaguely discern the flow of time.

"This is…"

Then he discovered something. Besides them, there were others fleeing the Titanic neighbourhood. Furthermore, the pursuers seemed to be a mix of different factions.

"…Found them."

After hearing the information, it became clear that the fugitives were a pair, one of whom appeared to be a Cyclops. Such a situation at this time couldn't be completely unrelated to their quarry; it could be Margomedari Brompton himself.

While the knowledge of a pair of individuals concerned him, this information itself was merely a rough accumulation of assumptions and speculations, and insisting on clarifying the details would be futile. The next step was to actually go there and verify the facts with his own eyes.

"Let's go."

He suddenly stood up. There were many things he was concerned about, and the problems he needed to solve piled up. But for now, he wanted to follow his own priorities.

For Feodor right now, negotiating with Margomedari Brompton was one of his highest priorities. Rather than putting this off, he might as well forget the pain in this body and the strange things inhabiting his head.

"…What's wrong?"

He came back to his senses. His gaze had unknowingly fixed on Lakish’s face.

"Nothing—ah, no," he said, looking away. "I was just a little mesmerised."

"Yes, yes, thank you for your simple, polite words."

Just as Feodor had hoped, Lakish wasn't shy or particularly self-conscious. She simply replied with a slight shrug.

### **Part 3 – The Woman Named Odette Gundakar**

They were led to the back door of a large mansion on the riverbank. Although the door was a little too small for Margomedari, he could just barely pass through by bending down and tilting his shoulders.

"Excuse me…"

They followed the girl leading the way, through what looked like a kitchen, and into a living room.

A woman sat on a cheap sofa. She had long silver hair and purple eyes, a gentle smile playing on her lips.

When she saw them enter, she stood up from the sofa and rushed over to hug the black-robed girl tightly.

"Rita, thank you so much\!"

"Od…Odetta, this is…uncomfortable…"

"I'm sorry, I asked you to do something so strange. Are you in danger? Are you scared? Did anyone strange talk to you?"

"Okay…okay\!"

The girl twisted her body awkwardly, breaking free from the woman's embrace and running out of the living room.

The woman watched her leave, then turned back shortly afterwards.

"She got away."

She stuck out her tongue and smiled.

"…Uh."

"It's been a long time, you two. I'm glad to see you're in good spirits."

She smiled gently. "Well, those were my relative's children. I really wanted to go greet you in person, but for various reasons I had to.”

“It wasn't convenient, so I asked her to go in my place. But then again, if I showed up suddenly, you two wouldn't have followed me, would you?” Some guilt fuelled her, but she spoke at a rapid pace.

"…senior Jessman."

"Ah, sorry, actually, my last name isn't Jessman anymore. I'm Odette Gundakar now. I got married a long time ago back home and changed my last name."

"Huh, is that so?" Naigrat was surprised.

Odette Jessman, now also known as Odette Gundakar, was an Imp and one of the people Naigrat knew while studying at the Academy. She was quite famous. At first glance, she seemed…although it's strange to say this…well-educated and dignified. However, within the student community at the time, she was nicknamed "witch" and "demon queen" (none of which were exaggerated). She was a woman with a perverse, twisted personality and a vicious nature. To her, lying was like breathing in, kidnapping like breathing out. I wonder how many classmates had been deceived by her outward gentleness and composure, leaving them with bitter regret.

What if, like her, a man with extraordinary support found his way around to her, and she even achieved the happiness of a normal person? Wouldn't that be something to be happy about? Naigrat thought, and then she said, "Congratulations—"

"By the way, he passed away five years ago."

"Uhhh…"

The words of sincere congratulations she had intended to offer were shot down mid-sentence. A moment's confusion, whether to celebrate the happy event or grieve over the happiness lost, stopped Naigrat’s thoughts. But the next moment, she realised that this confusion was exactly what Odette wanted. "—Um, senior Jess-… Odette, you're not just teasing me, are you?"

"Hehe, you're right."

Odette smiled with a pleasant yet wicked smile.

"Let me think, it's been about thirteen years since we last met. You seem to have grown quite a bit, but your reactions are still just as adorable, Naigrat Astartus."

"Really? I'm an adult now\! Don't add my father's name when you address me\!"

Naigrat suddenly turned to look at Margomedari, who had been unusually quiet.

"Gundakar…?" He muttered the surname thoughtfully.

Just as Naigrat was about to ask—

"By the way, would you like some tea? It’s Hydrangea’s No. 20 batch. You liked it, right, Naigrat?”

"Ah, yes." Her attention was drawn back at the perfect moment. "…You remember exactly what kind of tea people like."

"I'm an Imp, after all."

Odette placed the kettle on the small cylindrical stove.

"If you want to deceive someone, you have to understand them. What they like, what they dislike, what they can't tolerate, what they won't give up—"

Odette spoke as she adjusted the stove’s flame.

"There's no such thing as a 'universal lie that can deceive anyone.' Every deception is tailored to each individual. For us, a race that feeds on people’s hearts, this is our pride."

Naigrat thought it made sense.

If Imps like Odette feed on people’s hearts, then Trolls like her feed on human flesh. There's no universal cooking method or seasoning that can be used on all meats. For a Troll, understanding the piece of meat before them and cooking it the best way for each individual is a kind of pride.

If the two are similar, she had to agree to a certain extent.

 "…That was also a lie. Hehe."

*Hey, what's going on? Give my approval back\!*

"But I told that lie because I thought Naigrat would believe it. Listen, a lie is about gaining a firm grasp of someone's information and then deceiving them. Understanding their preferences, ways of thinking, and understanding is the most fundamental of all. Do you understand?"

"…Yes, absolutely."

She was not good at dealing with this person. One half of Naigrat believed this strongly, and the other half was exasperated to tears.

She suddenly thought of Aiseia. Of the adult fairy soldiers still alive, Aiseia was the oldest. Her always unpredictable personality, her blunt yet not fully truthful words, made her think she has some points in common with Odette.

Perhaps that child could give this trickster a good fight… No, if they were allowed to meet, they might even team up to make her cry. Just as Naigrat was contemplating this foolish thought…

"—I have a question for you, Odette Gundakar."

A deep, stern voice reached her ears.

There was no need to identify the person; it was the enormous man sitting right next to the sofa. Since there wasn't a chair for him, he'd simply plopped himself down on the carpet—Margomedari Brompton.

"What do you want to ask?"

"I don't recall receiving any notice for the reunion, and I certainly didn't send one myself. So, it's quite unusual for us to be here. Why are you here—no…"

The single eye narrowed, and after a moment's deliberation, he said, "What are you doing here?"

What did this question mean? Naigrat pondered. She didn't think the difference between the two sentences was significant enough to warrant a different question.

Odette chuckled.

"Dr. Brompton, as expected."

She pulled a slip of paper from her sleeve.

Margomedari’s expression changed noticeably. "…Where did you get that?"

"At your private residence, of course. Sorry for the mess." Odette shrugged.

"But it's not something I can do. We're competing with others, after all. We were a step ahead, but if we'd delayed any longer, the item would have been in the hands of the Winged Guard."

Naigrat had no idea what the two people were talking about.

"Senior…?"

"Before we talk about me, let's check on your current situation."

Odette sat down on the sofa.

"There are two types of pursuers: the Winged Guard, and the origins of the other are still unknown. Both sides are operating to capture Doctor Brompton. I suspect it's related to Doctor Brompton's special spirit tuning technique… Okay, that's it, isn't it?"

Naigrat thought for a moment and nodded. Although she didn't know what it was, Odette’s words were consistent with her current understanding of the situation.

Margomedari stared at Odette with his single eye, remaining silent and not answering.

"Doctor, please don't be silent. How would you rate my hypothesis?"

"I don't know the best answer, so I can't rate it." Margomedari said slowly.

Naigrat felt like he was lying.

And if even she could see through it, then this lie probably couldn't be hidden from the Imp before them.

"I have a suggestion."

Odette leaned forward slightly.

"Do you want to sell that tuning method?"

Margomedari shook his head. "To the remnants of Elpis?"

*—Huh?*

Naigrat thoughts froze.

"So, you know my husband?"

"He's a celebrity, after all. He was the vice-captain of the Elpis National Defense Force, and as the mastermind behind that ‘series of events’, he was accused of everything and ultimately executed."

"Yes, that Gundakar. He was a remarkable man, rising to the top of the organisation, committing evil deeds and being executed amidst the people's hatred. It's a way of life typical of Imps, but for he, a Stella, to have ended up living a more exciting life than any of us Imps…” She chuckled softly.

"So, Doctor, you think I inherited his legacy?"

"I think that possibility must be considered."

"You're right. But don't worry. My hometown may be Elpis, but a hometown is just that, a hometown. I am me, not part of any organisation. Although I know those so-called remnants, I have no contact with them anymore…"

Odette said "but," paused, and then continued:

"…putting this matter aside, I have an agreement with the higher-ups of the Noble Wings Empire. I will bring back the key to defending the Regul Aire—the Dug Weapons and the secrets of the Leprechauns."

"Huh?"

So, in short, what does this mean?

"Let me tell you one more thing. The group chasing you just now wasn't the Winged Guard, but my colleagues—the ones whose origins you didn't know. Oh, don't worry, I didn't tell them about this place. After all, if you want to deceive others, you should start with your own people."

She calmly said such a shameful thing with a face devoid of any guilt.

At this point, Naigrat couldn't even contain her shock.

"So, regarding my earlier speculation about 'unclear origins,' I actually know the answer. The Noble Wings Empire wanted to hire Margomedari Brompton, your former self, as a technical advisor. They knew brute force might be a problem, so they sent me along."

"I refuse."

"…I think you should reconsider. At least they should offer you better treatment than the current Winged Guard."

Ah, so—a belated question flashed through Naigrat’s mind. Dr. Margomedari Brompton was originally an ally of the Winged Guard and the Orlandri Trading Company. That was clearly the case, so why were Winged Guard soldiers now pursuing him? They were even holding gunpowder rifles against the doctor, and trying to force him. Why?

"Since you've seen that note, you should already understand why I answered that way, right?" Margomedari said with a wry smile.

"The current fairy tuning process we've made actually added a lot of unnecessary effort. Therefore, if we wanted to, we could significantly streamline the process, creating even more powerful adult fairy soldiers in a simpler and faster way. Anyone who knew the steps would choose that path. In other words, if we let anyone besides me know the tuning process, that's what would happen."

The one-eyed man slowly—with an exaggerated sigh, looked up at the ceiling. Compared to the one-eyed being’s size, the ceiling was far too low.

"But that path, that path alone, is one I absolutely forbid. No more adult fairies of that kind can be born."

"Really? I just don't understand. What are you afraid of at this point? So afraid, even adding 'unnecessary effort'? What's the point of setting up a defense? What kind of problems will adult fairy soldiers, who haven't gone through that kind of ‘effort’, face?"

Margomedari smiled faintly.

"You’ve already connected it to that term, right? I'm referring to the Night of Mourne."

He uttered the term as if in prayer.

"…I've never heard of it."

"In that case, it's best if you don't know. I've lived a long time, after all, and even those unrecorded moments are seared into my eyes and mind. It's not just me; the six people with knowledge of fairy tuning are all accomplices. The memory of that night has always terrified us—"

"—Can you tell me about that incident, too?"

It's unknown when that person appeared there. Everyone's gaze turned to and became fixed on a young man.

He had short silver hair and wore a black suit. His eye colour was obscured by his tinted glasses.

He was about fifteen years old. Another person Naigrat didn't recognize.

*(Probably around the same age as Tiat and Lakish…)*

Naigrat’s heart sank slightly as she thought of the two Leprechauns who had sallied forth and who she would never see again.

And just then…

"Feo… dor…?"

Beside her, Odette Jessman—no, Odette Gundakar—looked at the boy with an expression of disbelief.

This woman always maintained a calm demeanour, as if she saw through everything and had it all under control, but the expression on her face now was, at least for Naigrat, a new one.

"This is the first time I've seen you look like that, sister\! I've come all this way."

Seeing Odette’s expression—after the boy seemed to be calling her "sister"—, the boy spread his arms dramatically and saluted like a stage actor.

"Hello, everyone. Nice to meet you. I'm Feodor Jessman, the younger brother of Odette Gundakar."

He put on a show of cool, a broad smile on his face, and spoke aloud as if reciting a heroic tale:

"This time—"

*Woo-woo-woo-woo-woo\!*

The kettle on the small cylindrical stove made a sharp sound.

The boy's words were interrupted.

An awkward silence filled the room. "Ah, uh…"

Odette asked, seemingly listless.

"…Would you like some tea too? I'm about to brew No. 23 from Hydrangea."

"Ah, yes, I'll have some."

The boy, completely drained of energy, nodded docilely with a dazed expression.

 

†

 

No one in the living room noticed.

In the adjacent room, across the doorway, a young woman trembled slightly.

She wrapped herself tightly in a black robe, her face drooping even lower beneath her hood.

"Feodor…?"

She muttered the boy's name as if she were delirious with a fever.

"Liar… are you really… still alive…?"

### **Part 4 – Enjoying Trendy Desserts in a Trendy City**

In a trendy city, even the pastries are stylishly prepared.

Sitting in front of Tiat was a snow-white yogurt cake, drizzled with yellow syrup and garnished with green mint leaves.

It was hard to describe; it was like a work of art. The moment she poked the spoon in, it felt like she'd destroyed something precious, and a strange sense of guilt welled up. She brought the trembling cake into her mouth, resting it on the tip of her tongue.

"…\!?"

It tasted icy and sweet, with a hint of sweet and sour. This new taste made Tiat squirm uncontrollably.

She and Noft were enjoying a snack in a café overlooking the fountain.

Grick wasn't there; he remained at headquarters, discussing some complicated matters with the First Division's technical officer. While it seemed a little improper to let two fairies go out without their supervisor, no one had said anything so far… so it was just how it was for now. 

"Ugh, seriously\! This is so frustrating— I can't stand it\!"

Noft herself was clearly in a terrible mood as she dug into the pear tart with her fork. "Why is Naigrat considered a criminal? No matter how you think about it, it's strange. Rather than going through the trouble of kidnapping, she'd probably just burn and eat him right then and there."

*No, that's hard to say…* Tiat thought, but kept it to herself. "I’m telling you, it’s just a misunderstanding. Mr. Grick seems to be handling the matter right now. They'll surely understand soon."

"No, no, no, you're too naive… That person has a clingy, stubborn face. Once listed as a suspect, they'll be suspected to the bitter end until they die. That's *absolutely* what’s going to happen\!"

Noft opened her mouth wide as she settled a piece of the pear tart in her mouth before chewing on it. 

"…This is delicious," she declared solemnly.

"Please give me a piece," Tiat demanded without hesitation.

After negotiating, the two decided to trade a bite of yogurt cake for a bite of pear tart.

The menu beside her read "Manager's Recommendation," accompanied by a drawing of a donut set. It looked truly delicious. After all, this was a rare opportunity, and she was eager to try it. She debated for a long time, but ultimately chose the yogurt cake.

She always felt, truly always felt, that even if she ate the donuts, something would be slightly off. It's not that she had any grievances against her tablemate, Noft. No, that wasn't it… but that was just what it felt like. 

*…Why am I making excuses, and who am I telling them to?*

"I hope the real culprit can be caught soon and the misunderstanding clears up. Also, if that huge… Doctor Ma… Margo or something is safe, that'd be great."

"That's right. It's really frustrating that we can't catch him ourselves."

Noft chewed a bite and said, "This is delicious too\! Give me another bite."

"I can't give you any more. The rest is all mine." Tiat replied.

"Hey, what's with the attitude? You won't listen to me, your senior?"

"No matter who it’s against, there are always things that you just cannot give up."

The plate was cleared out.

"You must be anxious too, right? After all, you flew all the way here."

"Yeah, sort of."

Noft poured milk into her teacup until it was almost filled to the brim.

"…I feel like I always end up thinking about what happened during that time."

"What time?"

Noft slowly lifted the cup, brought the rim to her lips, and began to sip. "It's about when Kutori was obsessed with that Second Enchanted Weapons Technician." There was a note of nostalgia in her voice as she rested her elbows on the table, gazing out beyond the fountain plaza. 

"I just can't understand what it's like to fall in love with a man. I never understood why she smiled at the end."

"…Senior?"

"But it can't be helped, right? Fairies are just like that. The so-called men and women… Those genders exist for the sole purpose of reproduction, don't they? That has nothing to do with us, right?"

Even if Tiat tried to get her approval, she didn't know what to say.

"Well, but what about Mr. Grick?"

"Huh?"

"Although we're of different races, he's been by your side as a partner for years. It's a relationship of trust… so it should be pretty solid, right?"

"Oh, no, no. I don't think it's the kind of relationship you're thinking of." Noft shook her head. "Besides, the Borgles don't have a culture of lovers or couples. A child born to someone in the clan is raised by everybody in the clan. At that moment, all elders are parents, and all younglings are children. That’s why their surnames are the names of their clan, not their parents, see?"

"Oh."

Judging from the frank expression on Noft’s face as she spoke, it didn’t seem like she was hiding any shyness.

"If I asked you who your favourite man in the world is, what would you say?"

"Well, if that's the question, it would definitely be that big brother of ours," Noft replied immediately.

"Ah, just as I thought."

*That kind of relationship doesn't seem all that bad*, Tiat thought.

However, it was a different kind of relationship than the one Kutori-senior and Willem had, which was a relationship between adults in a different sense. Tiat thought it was cool, beautiful, and something she longed for. 

"It’s just that, if you ask whether it's the same kind of the fluttery, euphoric feeling that Kutori or you have right now—it does indeed seem a little different."

"Isn't that great? I think that's pretty good, too."

“Ahahahaha,” they both laughed heartily.

"Wait a minute."

"Hmm?" Noft blinked.

"Why do you bring that up I mean please don't compare me to my senior, no I mean being compared to my senior is an honour in itself but this is different. Feodor and I don't have that kind of relationship we hate each other deeply whether as a person or as a mission he's just my enemy\!"

"Really?" Noft smiled mischievously.

Although she had fired back swiftly, Noft paid her no real attention.

"Please don't give me that gentle, 'Oh, how insincere\!' smile; it's irritating."

"Ah, Tiat, you're so adorable."

"No I told you it's different\!"

Just as Tiat was about to protest further…

"—Ah."

She saw a large transportation vehicle powered by an internal combustion engine rumbling across the square.

On its platform sat at least ten imposingly armed soldiers. She also saw large gunpowder rifles—each as long as an arm—resting on their shoulders.

"That's…"

"As you expected, it's the task force to rescue Dr. Margomedari."

Tiat turned and saw Grick Graycrack raise a hand.

“Yo\!” he greeted. "It’d be ideal if this can be resolved peacefully. However, if the kidnappers were to resist, it wouldn’t be possible to suppress them without sufficient military force—hence those heavily armed soldiers."

"This…" Tiat was speechless. 

The kidnapper mentioned in this context, based on what was discussed earlier, must be Naigrat. She was certainly not someone that ordinary soldiers could subdue, but…

"Hey, I know what you want to say. But even with a bit of enhanced armament, they won’t stand a chance against that Naigrat, right?"

No, that's not the case. But it's not like Tiat can say that she didn’t think that way as well. 

"Actually, we've also speculated about a possible battle with spies from the Noble Wings Empire. Seriously, the world is starting to get turbulent…"

*The Noble Wings Empire.*

Come to think of it, that black goat-head First Officer seemed to have mentioned it. It's an aristocratic nation that links Floating Islands 6 through 9 together as its territory. Throughout the history of Regul Aire, this nation has repeatedly attacked neighbouring islands—but it was suppressed by the Winged Guard each time. 

"Oh? So, you mean, the Empire might be looking for an opportunity to seize that huge old man? Even if it means confronting the Winged Guard?"

"We can't discount that possibility. I heard that ever since the uprising in Elpis five years ago, the Noble Wings Empire and Hydrangea Tea Country have been actively trying to keep each other in check."

"Ah…" Noft sighed, and looked up at the sky.

"I can't stand it. They're all like this—they just love causing trouble for their neighbors, don’t they?"

"Well, you can’t quite put it that way."

Tiat ignored their conversation and instead stared blankly at the transport vehicle as it departed. As she gazed, she searched her memories.

She had seen those gunpowder rifles carried by the soldiers.

In preparation for the battle against the Eleventh Beast, many weapons were transported to Floating Island 38\. Some were potentially useful, while there were also weapons that were quite baffling. Mixed in with these weapons was a new type of gunpowder rifle—a portable firearm capable of inflicting the greatest devastation. It was this very weapon that the soldiers were carrying. If Tiat remembered correctly, its development name was the "Pupille Gorger."

According to the manual, this gunpowder rifle had enhanced close-range penetration—even capable of piercing thin walls. Due to its high price, difficulty in management, and limited utility, the entire Winged Guard had very few of them. Yet, every soldier on the transport vehicle was armed with one of these weapons… *What kind of urban battle were they preparing for?*

This outfit, indeed, looked as if it was prepared for the sole purpose of killing the capture target, the Cyclops—

"—Tiat?"

"Ah, huh? What's wrong?" She came to her senses. 

"Grick said we could order another dessert as an apology for waiting for him. What do you want?"

"Ah… Okay\!"

Tiat cast aside her fanciful thoughts and faced reality… which was "a soft, fluffy, creamy cake with seasonal colours."

Yes, now was the time to enjoy this incredibly delicious cake and forget all those unpleasant thoughts.

Having made up her mind, she turned her gaze away from the departing transport vehicle and onto the menu.

### **Part 5 – The Ogre Tea Party**

"…Isn’t it about time you let me go?"

Lakish complained, seemingly distressed.

"No."

Like a petulant child, the female Troll—Naigrat—rejected the request.

Naigrat's arms clenched around Lakish—as tight as they could get—and she showed no sign of letting go. It was said that a Troll's arms were strong enough to easily break the spine of a large bear. Since this situation obviously didn't happen, it certainly meant that she wasn't using her full strength—but she didn't seem to be controlling it either.

"I heard earlier that your magic power went out of control and you fell into a coma, never to wake up. It made me cry so much. So, I want you to return all your tears to me."

"Coma…? Ugh, it's… so uncom… uncomfortable, my bones… creaking—please let go…"

"Excuse me, Miss Naigrat."

Someone gently patted her shoulder from behind.

Naigrat turned around with a half-crying face.

"Odette’s younger brother."

She addressed him somewhat disrespectfully. But, of course, it was the truth.

"My name is Feodor Jessman. Due to certain circumstances, I temporarily served as the supervisor of four people, including Miss Lakish."

"Huh… oh? Oh, oh, oh, so the officer in charge of those children is…"

"Yes, I was in that position until about last week. Now, except for Miss Lakish, there should be someone else who has taken over for the others."

He wasn't lying. He simply left out the fact that "he's no longer in charge because he betrayed the Winged Guard, and Lakish is considered a deserter for being here right now."

"…Are those children doing well? Are they causing you any trouble?"

"Well, well… at least they're nice people." He vaguely answered only one of the questions.

"…So, Mr. Feodor Jessman, senior military officer of the Fourth rank, what brings you to a place like this?"

Odette interrupted. "You can tell we're a bit busy right now. After tea, can you take her back?"

"Sister, I could say about half of those same words back to you. We came here specifically to see Dr. Margomedari, but why are you here as well?"

"Because I stole some secrets from the Noble Wings Empire’s intelligence team… Ah."

At this point, Odette placed her hand on her forehead.

"So that's how it is. Feodor, could the source of your intelligence this time be the intelligence broker Nax Selzel?"

"…You even know about that guy? You're right."

"As I expected. He often secretly embezzles the Empire Intelligence Team's investigation records as a source of supply. In other words, the information he sells to you and the information we receive come from the same source."

*—Oh, so that's how it is. What an unpleasant overlap.*

He suddenly felt a headache.

It seemed that important figures were being murdered one after another. This series of murders had become the subject of an intelligence blockade, nicknamed the "Blackened Dagger," and a covert investigation was underway.

The confirmed victims were, in order, Lieutenant General Iwa, a different senior military officer, the strategic advisor to the Orlandri Trading Company, and the vice president of the Collinadiluche Comprehensive Treatment Centre.

The commonality immediately apparent during the investigation was, of course, their identities. Each held a prominent position within the Winged Guard or had previously held such a position. Furthermore, they were all involved in the operation of the weapon "Leprechaun"—specifically the construction, improvement, and operation of its adult tuning system.

This information could be revealed by examining the documents currently extant within the Winged Guard.

However, that was all that could be learned.

On the table lay freshly brewed black tea and a plate full of cookies. "…Have things come to this?" Feodor dropped four sugar cubes into a cup of black tea and sipped the liquid, which had almost turned to sugar water, muttering to himself. *Mmm, really delicious.*

"I've only been away from the army for a few days, but I feel completely disconnected from the world… So while I don't know the reason, the Winged Guard speculates that Dr. Margomedari is their next target, right?"

Odette nodded slightly in agreement.

"Based on the intelligence we have so far, what do you know?"

"Hmm… Well, just a few things. But they're all within the range that you should already know."

"Tell me. I want to know how capable you are now."

He pondered for a moment. How much sense would it make to express his inner thoughts at this moment? What cards should be hidden, what should be exaggerated, what should be probed?

After thinking it over, he decided it was best to speak honestly now.

*There’s really no other way.* Feodor sighed softly. "The serial killer is either the Winged Guard or the high-ranking officials of the Orlandri Trading Company."

Margomedari raised his pale face in surprise.

Naigrat nearly dropped her teacup—but managed to catch herself. She glanced back and forth between Feodor and Margomedari.

Odette snorted, as if in a state of boredom. "What's the basis for your theory?"

"The assumption that Dr. Margomedari’s life is targeted is strange. Every faction, including the Noble Wings Empire, wants him. They must be hoping to capture this doctor, the ultimate authority in fairy tuning technology, without harming him in the slightest. This is perfectly clear, yet the military has concluded that the doctor might be killed. This means they have some basis for this conclusion, or perhaps another reason."

He spoke as he picked up the milk jug. "Also, one more thing. Before I came here, I saw the equipment of the Winged Guard wandering the streets, and I noticed that the ‘Pupille Gorger’ was standard equipment."

Everyone present looked confused as to what they were.

"It's a large gunpowder rifle with a shortened range and increased lethality, specifically designed to kill races with unnaturally strong vitality. It's too powerful to be used against the Empire’s spies. I heard that even Trolls can be reduced to minced meat depending on where they're struck, so their target might be…"

"You’re… lying…"

Naigrat’s eyes widened. It was a reasonable reaction. No one with normal sensibilities could withstand such a direct onslaught of murderous intent.

"Making beautiful minced meat takes a lot of effort\! I hate those haphazard cooking methods\!"

"Uh…"

*Uh, what? Was that what she was angry about?*

"I think," Margomedari asked weakly, "that the military is urgently implementing countermeasures simply because Little Nai is the one who kidnapped me. Perhaps there's no other purpose behind this."

"Impossible. Miss Naigrat has only been pursued by the Winged Guard for less than half a day, right? The Pupille Gorgers aren't the kind of weapons that can be deployed in large quantities immediately. The reason they're being used now as a matter of course is that they've already prepared them, ready for immediate use. I'm afraid—"

He looked at the puffed-up Naigrat.

"—for the Winged Guard, Miss Naigrat's involvement is a fortunate surprise. This way, they can openly use the weapon they want to use against Titanic targets."

"The weapons. The unnatural speed with which they handled the arrest of Miss Naigrat and their lack of any intention to retreat depending on the situation confirm my suspicions. In other words, summarising the above—" He gulped down his tea.

“Their true purpose is to disguise the killing of the Cyclops—who cannot be killed by ordinary means—as an accidental one. This explanation is the easiest to understand.” Everyone’s attention focused on Margomedari.

“At first, I thought a high-ranking official had been caught with evidence of malfeasance, and the doctor was a witness or accomplice, so they wanted to kill him to silence him. However, judging by the current situation, that doesn’t seem to be the case,” Feodor said. 

As long as he continued to eliminate one possibility after another, at least the remaining options would get closer and closer to the truth.

 "The Winged Guard is an organisation dedicated to 'fighting those who threaten the survival of the Regul Aire.' There's no distinction between good and evil. In other words, you—and perhaps the four people who were assassinated—though undisclosed, are also considered such a threat… If that's the case, then the current situation makes sense."

Margomedari remained silent. He lowered his head again, his massive shoulders slumping heavily. His silence, more convincing than any words, confirmed Feodor’s assumption.

"Senior…" Naigrat muttered worriedly.

*Pa-pa-pa\!* Untimely applause erupted from the audience.

Everyone's attention now focused on Odette.

"You're correct. It's terrifying\! Once you're targeted by the Winged Guard, there's virtually no escape anywhere in Regul Aire. Even running around like we're doing now has its limits. Even if we leave this Floating Island, we still won't be able to completely escape the Winged Guard’s clutches."

*What should we do then?* She smiled and tilted her head slightly.

*Ah, I see.* Feodor understood completely. In other words, his sister was trying to steer the conversation in this direction. To survive, they had to flee to a closed country and hide out from the Winged Guard. And right now, there was a country that perfectly met these requirements, eagerly awaiting a response—

"…May I correct that? It's not as if the entire Winged Guard has unanimously decided to kill us. I think this must be the order from Lieutenant General Iwa of Rosy Claw," as if shaking something off, as if giving up, Margomedari raised his head. 

"But Lieutenant General Iwa of Rosy Claw was…"

"Yes, he was the first of the five to die, confirmed to be the first victim in the serial murder case. Given his personality, he must have ordered that we be dealt with in this manner before committing suicide. His final instructions were probably to find a reason to eliminate all five of us—to prevent the technology used to manipulate fairy spirits from remaining in this world. So… well, I've finally made up my mind. After this, I'll surrender to the Winged Guard."

"You’re going to seek death?"

"I've lived long enough. When I think of all the lives I've manipulated so far, I've lived too long. And I saw the faces of old friends in the end. Now, Rosy Claw and the others must be waiting for me to come."

"Senior, is your resolve and resolution…", Naigrat’s voice was calm, but it sounded as if all emotion had been suppressed, "…more important than Almita and the others—more important than the future of all the children?"

"…………"

After a moment's hesitation, the Cyclops simply turned away helplessly.

Naigrat fell silent. Faced with what could be described as a heartless response, she neither rebuked nor questioned.

"Dr. Margomedari," Feodor's voice pierced the heavy atmosphere. "I'd like to ask you directly. You are the ultimate authority on fairies and past-life personality encroachment… Isn't that correct?"

"There's only one such person in this world. How can there be such a thing as an ultimate authority…" he wondered, self-mockery evident in his muttering.

"I have two requests for your help."

"No. I told you I won’t perform fairy tuning anymore."

"I've heard that. But that's my second request. I'd like you to grant me another request first."

*What does he mean by that?* Margomedari looked up, puzzled. 

"From what you just said, my understanding is that restarting the tuning pipeline for new fairy soldiers is taboo. But that doesn't mean that all the already-tuned adult fairy soldiers must be disposed of, right?"

"Yes… I suppose so."

"Then, please… examine one… fairy."

He turned his gaze to Naigrat. Or rather, to the (for some reason) exhausted girl in her arms.

"Lakish Nyx Seniolis."

Lakish, whose name was called, looked at him in confusion.

"Me?"

“Yes, I'm talking about you.” He nodded at her. "She opened the Fairy Gate once, causing her personality to collapse. Then, through some unknown process, she awoke and is now able to move around conscious and clear-headed like this… But if we don't know the cause, we don't know when this miracle will end. I want to do something before her mind collapses again."

"Feodor, you…"

He pushed back the accusing voice without even a glance.

The Cyclops stared at Feodor, and Feodor stared back through his glasses.

"This matter concerns the life of the girl currently here. Unless it touches your taboos, please agree."

"…That's true. If that's all, surely the Rosy Claw wouldn’t be angry, right?"

A sense of relief spread within Feodor.

"But, speaking of this—while it's not a price, there's one thing… Yes, just one thing I'd like you to help me with." The Cyclops raised a thick finger. "I'm afraid I can't return to that house, but if possible, there's something I don't want to leave there—and I was hoping that you could get it for me."

"…There are still a lot of people wandering around outside… including *someone's* friends."

He glared at Odette sharply, and Odette looked away.

Although his sister was an ally of the Empire, she had no intention of reporting Margomedari's discovery to the intelligence agents. It was likely due to their own operatives vying for credit, but that works out just as well.

"Compared to the others, I think you going would be the safest. Of course, I won't force you."

Feodor hadn't admitted that he was being pursued by the Winged Guard. So, in Margomedari's opinion, Feodor seemed the one with the most freedom of movement among the members present. He glanced at Lakish (still being preyed upon by Naigrat), only to see her shrug, seemingly unconcerned with his decision.

"I see. So, what exactly are you taking back—"

"Hey, wait a minute." A voice suddenly interrupted.

He glanced over impatiently. Honestly, his sister was always the type who couldn't read the mood.

"Why? Let me be clear, this is a deal between us. Don't try to interfere, sister."

"That's not my intention. Since it's still dangerous out there, at least bring a guard."

With that, Odette clapped her hands lightly toward the living room.

"Are you listening? Come in."

Someone's shaky breath drifted from outside the door.

"If you don't come in, I'll call your name. Is that okay?"

The doorknob turned, and the door slowly slid open. Appearing on the other side was a fragment of the night sky, dissolving into droplets with a *drip*—

—As if.

 No, it was a petite figure, completely concealed in a black robe and a mask of the dead.

"Who is that?"

"A very important companion of mine… you could say. This has nothing to do with the Empire. There's no need to worry about any ties there, nor is there any debt of gratitude involved. I simply didn't want my beloved brother to be put in danger alone."

Instantly, everyone in the living room looked at Odette with suspicion.

"…I knew you all would think so."

Odette gave a weak smile, then spoke in a hypocritical, uneasy voice. "The Imps really have it hard. They're just born this way… at crucial moments, even family bonds are questioned."

*No, it's just because of your usual behaviour*—that's the kind of look Feodor gave Odette.

*Huh, it's not because of your usual behaviour?*—that's the kind of look Naigrat gave Odette.

*Well, it's just due to your usual behaviour*—that's the kind of look Margomedari gave Odette.

Lakish sighed with an air of indifference.

Only the figure in the black robe remained silent, and instead fixed a steady yet calm gaze on Feodor from behind the mask of the dead.

†

### **Part 7 – Companion in the Dark**

Feodor's head stabbed with pain.

Since the night Lakish woke up, this slight ache had been with him constantly. If it interfered with his concentration, it would be extremely disadvantageous for him—a rebel and fugitive. But it was much better now.

As long as he didn’t peer into the mirror—as long as he didn’t see that guy's face—the pain wouldn’t worsen. It would ease a bit. He’d been doing this ever since he discovered it.

From somewhere in the distance, the sound of gunpowder gunfire spread.

The spies from the Winged Guard and the Noble Wings Empire's spies were engaged in a skirmish. While both sides were on a mission to capture Dr. Margomedari, they couldn't ignore each other's presence. If they met while searching the streets, a fight would be inevitable.

"So close—better stay away from that place," Feodor whispered, removing his glasses and putting them in his breast pocket.

Maintaining a low crouch, he leaped high—from the roof of the multi-story house to the one of the opposite house across the street. He rolled to cushion the impact of his landing, then silently stood up and ran away. The armed groups were tracking the Cyclops. Therefore, they naturally weren't wary of this acrobatic manoeuvring, something the Cyclops couldn't possibly accomplish.

Beside Feodor, a petite figure silently followed him.

## **Chapter 4 – "Advancing on Distinct Paths, this is——A" / “-going separate ways-”**

### **Part 1 – Afterward**

Three days had passed since that night.

In some ways, they had been quite peaceful.

Lakish had been sleeping more. According to Margomedari, given the complex situation of multiple, fragmented personalities, it was natural for her body and mind to need some rest.

Or rather, she had been sleeping too little, perhaps forcing herself to stay on edge…

Hearing this, Feodor felt even more guilty than worried.

The Orcs (?) were responsible for procuring the food, while Naigrat was responsible for preparing it. Although she said something like, "I don't know if it would suit boys' tastes," her meals were incredibly delicious and impeccable. Especially the various dishes incorporating mutton and its delicate seasonings. Thinking of Tiat and the others, who had grown up eating such fine food, made him even jealous.

Feodor continued to roam the streets day and night.

The Orcs’ connections, financial resources, and intelligence-gathering capabilities were currently being fully utilised. However, even this alone left many shortcomings, not to mention the various covert operations that couldn't be delegated. Ultimately, it was best to personally traverse, witness, and execute.

Occasionally, he would return to his hideout, eat while looking at everyone's faces, and then head out again.

He hurriedly began to formulate a plan to escape with Margomedari and the others, as well as other preparations.

![][image7]

The sun shone warmly at midday.

Near the fountain in the square, the Falcon children were feeding the pigeons. Every time they scattered crushed roasted beans, the pigeons would flock to them. The children laughed happily, scattering beans once more, and then another bird flew down from somewhere in the sky.

Feodor sat at one end of a four-seater bench.

He took the leafy lamb wrap he'd bought from a nearby vendor out of its paper bag and took a bite. The leafy vegetables were soft, while the lamb was a bit cold and tough. He'd heard it was a local specialty, so he'd bought it to try, but the taste wasn't quite what he'd expected.

But then, after all, that's what a specialty is. It wasn't terrible, after all, and he was already starving. He took a big bite, devouring nearly half the remaining piece, and then finished the whole thing in three more bites. Then, he crumpled the rest of the paper bag into a small ball and put it in his pocket.

"—You used the Imps Eyes power on that child, didn't you?"

A voice spoke to him, but he wasn't startled. He had guessed she'd be coming for him soon, which was why he'd come to this place alone.

"Yeah."

He nodded, his gaze shifting to the other end of the bench, where he caught sight of the elegantly seated profile of Odette Gundakar—his elder sister.

"And it seems quite powerful, doesn't it?"

There are all sorts of creatures in this world. There are lizards that blend into the surrounding landscape to hide themselves, fish that release lightning from their bodies just before being preyed upon, and rats that emit a foul odour to keep enemies away. Small animals, especially those preyed upon by larger beasts, often possess these kinds of special abilities.

The Imp Eyes power possessed by the Imps might be one of these abilities. When making eye contact at very close range, they can exert psychological influence, lowering their hostility and vigilance, temporarily tricking them into believing they are a close friend. It's a form of hypnosis. It wasn't a particularly powerful ability—rather, it was simply useless.

Furthermore, the conditions for its use were quite demanding. Not only did it require close eye contact, but the surroundings also had to be dimly lit, and both parties had to be in a particular state of mind (Stressed? Delirious?). How, exactly, could one drag a hostile and wary opponent into such a situation? Furthermore, even if all the conditions were overcome, the success rate wouldn't be very high. Who would want to use such a power?

The requirements and the results were unequal. It was truly impractical.

…Feodor had long thought as such.

"Yes, it's even more powerful than I imagined."

The power now enchanting Lakish's mind couldn't be described as mere hypnosis. It was clear that this power had made her extremely dependent on Feodor.

"Indeed, you're truly my little brother. You're a genius."

"Okay, stop saying that."

"Don't say that. Let me praise you. It's rare to get the chance to praise my silly brother so fully."

"…I mean it. Stop it."

The elder sister looked genuinely proud, and he averted his gaze from her.

"You have something to say, don't you? Beating around the bush isn't like you, sis."

A pause.

"Kill that kid now."

Suddenly, a dozen pigeons gathered in the square took flight simultaneously.

The shed grey feathers, bathed in the sunlight, shimmered with a rainbow of colours.

"You've probably vaguely realised, haven't you? The true power of those Eyes isn't some convenient hypnotic technique. It's just a weakened form of that power that's being perceived that way. It's fundamentally different," Odette said calmly. "Exchanging fragments of one's own soul with that of another—this is the power characteristic our ancestors pride themselves on."

"Ancestors?"

"Indeed. The ancient Imps were hybrids born from humans and hostile spirits… demons. Though bound to flesh through generations, their origins were closer to spirits."

Feodor was surprised.

The origin of the Imps wasn't shocking in itself. They were a type of demon (Ogre?), a race formed over five hundred years ago through Emnetwyte mutation, having eventually separated enough to become its own race. While not quite common knowledge, it was widely known.

The fact that the Imps were akin to incarnated, flesh-bound spirits was new to him, and it struck him as somewhat surprising. This was because it was very similar to the existence of the Leprechauns he knew.

"Breaking the mental boundary between yourself and the other, merging them together. That's the power of our Eyes. On a small scale, the effect is simply a sense of shared connection between the two… In effect, it only creates a slight sense of closeness."

Odette’s voice was stiff.

"However, what happens if more fragments of the mind are exchanged? The five senses and memories begin to blend, blurring the lines between emotion and thought. While convenient in various ways, it's also a dangerous state. If left unchecked, your own personality will corrupt, crumble, and ultimately disappear."

Feodor chuckled subconsciously.

"What's so funny?"

"Huh… ah, huh?"

As she asked, Feodor realised the corner of his mouth was crooked.

He touched it with his hand to confirm. Indeed, Feodor Jessman was smiling.

"…You'll suffer from auditory and visual hallucinations. When alone, you'll see people around you, even conversing with them. This is a warning sign of the end."

He covered his mouth, suppressing a smile.

So, auditory and visual hallucinations are warning signs of the end? That's a puzzling question.

He used his Imp Eyes not only on Lakish Nyx Seniolis, but also on the Dead Black Agate, the dark-haired man in the mirror. He probably didn't properly contain his Eyes power after using it on Lakish. In the darkness, he and the Black Agate met eyes, and it was probably at that moment that the Eyes reactivated, mixing their minds.

"The solution is simple: just kill the person. You can't maintain a merged state with someone who has lost their mind. While it will take some time to recover, you can regain your own mind."

He snorted in response. "Is this your own experience?" he asked.

"Yes," he received a simple answer.

He found it ironic.

A heart shattered, a personality confused, and then his very existence gradually faded, vanished, fading into nothingness.

Although the cause and process were different, wasn't this just like the Leprechauns? It happened to him, though. He had acted to deny those children the right to live, and now he was taking a step towards a similar outcome. Furthermore, this power and this current situation might even affect the life of Miss Lakish.

Things were getting complicated, he thought.

The instinctive fear of his own disappearance also surged. He felt a strong sense of loss, as if he were passing through the bench and the ground, plummeting into the earth.

And then, too, a feeling of joy was evident within him.

This fear must be the same as the Leprechauns. He felt himself getting a little closer to the figures of the women fighting in the hazy distance.

That was why he smiled.

"So? Did you come here specifically to give me advice?"

"Well, that's part of the point. I consider myself a gentle sister, after all, and I still care about my brother's health."

Hahaha, as expected of an orthodox Imp, able to tell lies so calmly that you couldn't help but believe them. He needed to learn this skill, too.

"The next topic is this. This time, I'd like you to help me with Dr. Margomedari."

"I don't want to."

"Why? Isn't it your goal to perform tuning on the adult fairy? Then, you should also know that there is no other way. If this continues, he will be killed by the Winged Guard."

"That would really be a headache."

"In that case…"

"Are you asking me to use those fairies as weapons for the Noble Wings Empire and then discard them?"

"…Yes, that's right. And that's probably what you want."

"Oh?" He frowned, urging her to continue.

"The Noble Wings Empire is very greedy. Once they obtain effective weapons, they will immediately use them as a weapon of aggression. If it's enough power to eliminate the Winged Guard’s interference, then it goes without saying. And that would also be perfect for your original goal. You want to 'reduce the number of floating islands', right?"

"Yes, that's right—"

He yawned. He definitely didn't find this topic boring, but he wanted to talk about something lighter next. "…Feodor?"

"I want to talk a little about the past. Sister, do you remember Marga?" he asked.

Marga Medicis. That was the name of Feodor's fiancée, once a noble daughter of an Elpis family. When they first met, Feodor was ten and Marg was seven. Both families naturally hoped they would develop a relationship, but at the time, they completely ignored their families' expectations. They were like family—like a little sister and her older brother, whose affection gradually deepened.

"Yes—of course I remember."

Odette nodded, her voice a little stiff.

"I don't like children. If you show them even the slightest bit of kindness, they'll immediately cling to me. They love to crawl around, cling to me, and bite me. No matter what I'm thinking, they don't care."

"Feodor—"

"And they’ll disappear without a second's notice. They won't even give me a chance to say goodbye," Feodor muttered.

"I was really happy. Yes, I admit it. Those times with Marga were incredibly joyful. Even so, I can't remember what her expression was the last time I saw her. I can't even tell if she was crying or laughing."

He couldn't speak properly.

He couldn't even control the emotion that should have been in his voice.

"Despite this, I thought I'd forgotten. Fighting for justice, carrying on my brother-in-law's unfinished work, if I lived that way, I'd forget about it. But…"

He paused.

"But no, I keep falling into the same old mistakes. Children clinging to me, crawling on me, clinging to me, biting me. There was happiness, and joy, but I wasn’t able stop them. Apple is gone, and I didn't even get a chance to say goodbye. And I can't remember what her expression was the last time I saw her."

He paused, then slowly raised his head to look up at the sky. "—So, I no longer want to send them away."

"Feodor, you…"

"I know what I said was absurd and irrational. I was just speaking out of impulse. I know all that."

But despite that—

In the end, it was all because he had vowed to change the world for the sake of his ideals.

And once he found his ideals, he couldn't let it go.

"So, anyone who intends to use them as weapons—whether it's the Winged Guard, the Noble Wings Empire, or even themselves—are my enemy."

Time moved slowly.

Odette stood up.

"I'm so disappointed in you."

"What a coincidence\! Me too."

He gave a wry smile at the cold voice. "I have no interest in your childish ideals. We're taking the doctor away. If you try to interfere, I'll kill you without mercy."

"You wish\! I will never hand him over to you, sister."

Feodor also stood up.

He turned his back to Odette and took a step forward.

"Can I ask you one last question?"

He paused.

Asking questions just as someone is about to die is truly despicable. Is this a tactic designed to pounce when the tension in the conversation has eased, to draw out the person's true colours? Never mind.

"What do you want to ask?"

Even so, he had nothing to worry about. After all, he had already confessed his true feelings to her. Feodor had no secrets that would be disturbing if they were revealed.

"If…"

Odette’s voice was hesitant, as if to act out something.

"If Rita were still alive… would you want to see her again?"

"Huh?"

He felt the question was truly cruel. There's a kind of hope where just the assumption, the contemplation of possibilities, is painful. Her question fell into that category.

"I cannot meet her." Feodor shrugged exaggeratedly. Now that their backs were turned, he knew his sister couldn’t see his face no matter what he did. "The gentle older brother she loved, the one who always stayed by her side, her fiancé, is gone. Now tainted with something filthy, how can I face her?"

"Is that so…?" She felt dejected. "You all do say that."

*You all?* Feodor, confused by what she meant, turned away.

However, Odette didn't seem to intend to say anything more. Her figure had already faded, about to disappear into the crowd.

Continuing and ending a conversation without permission was indeed very much like her sister's style. Unreasonable and wilful, not allowing others to see through her thoughts, and her thoughts were never good. She had always been like this. She hadn’t changed. 

"…Hmm?"

He thought he saw a winged figure approach Odette.

Even if he tried to see clearly, after blinking, all he could see was the throng of people.

"Nax?”

Thinking of the wings, Feodor couldn't help but blurt out the name of his Falcon friend.

But of course, that was impossible. Putting aside his side job, his main job was a private in the Fifth Division, and he was probably groaning under the weight of military duties on Floating Island 38 right now.

To say it was an illusion caused by a merged mind… wasn't right. He hadn't used his Imp Eyes on Nax, and he didn't sense him nearby. Perhaps his mind was just tired, creating an illusion.

"Pull yourself together, I suppose."

He reconsidered the weight of the fact that he was "an enemy of my sister." The so-called Imps are those who cannot be trusted even as allies, yet become extremely dangerous once they become enemies. This sister, unlike the marginally qualified Feodor Jessman, is a pure and orthodox Imp.

He had just declared war on a truly formidable opponent; he couldn't let his guard down any longer.

Feodor patted his cheeks, energising himself.
