### **Part 2 – Two People Who Don't Love Each Other**

The moment he looked at the calendar, his anxiety grew.

The time until the battle on Floating Island 38 was running out. When that day arrived, the three weapons—Tiat, Collon, and Panival—would be used for their original purposes as fairy soldiers.

Before then, he had to find a way to resolve the issue with the Fairy Warehouse, then tell them about it, so that they would accept the certainty that "even if they didn't sacrifice themselves, the younger fairies would be able to survive safely," overturning their deeply ingrained conviction to accept death. Therefore…

"You can take the airship we mentioned last time."

When he heard this announcement from the beautiful Orc woman, he nearly leaped up with the energy of an explosion.

The "last time" referred to the smuggling ship. Compared to the airship Feodor had taken when he arrived at this floating island, the smuggling ship was even more concealed. A Cyclops was already conspicuous, and if the destination became known, it would be pointless.

The Winged Guard had also increased security in the harbour area over the past few days, which had cost them a considerable amount of time. However, there was still time. As long as there was time, there was a way to solve any problem. He would find a way.

Whether it was Tiat, Collon, Panival, or Lakish, he would never send them to the battlefield.  

"So, we can prepare to leave\!"

He rushed into the room, announcing loudly. Having stayed up all night for days, he was perhaps somewhat unhinged. Margomedari and Naigrat’s shoulders trembled with fear, then they looked at him.

"Preparations for the flight are complete. I want to depart before dawn, so please be prepared. The Orcs will continue to support us, so for overly heavy belongings please consider buying new ones at our destination—what's the matter?"

They exchanged a glance.

"Nothing… I see. Everything's ready, huh?"

Margomedari rose from his custom-made chair.

"Feodor, can I ask you a question? I know now's not the best time, but if possible, I'd like to confirm your opinion."

"What's the question?"

"If the peace of Regul Aire were weighed against the life of little Lakish, which side would you choose?"

—What?

"Is this a psychological test? Something that’ll say you're sexually repressed or whatnot?"

"Perhaps something like that, but it won't lead to any conclusions about sexuality."

He thought for a moment. It was just a thought.

"I'd choose Lakish."

"…I thought so. But why?"

"For two reasons. The first is, I don’t give a damn about peace in Regul Aire. It's better for the world to face a more tangible threat. Everyone must truly experience fear, hurt, and preparation before learning to fight. Otherwise, the children forced to endure hurt and battle will receive nothing in return. I can't accept their efforts going unrewarded, unnoticed. This resentment is deeply rooted in my heart."

Margomedari was silent, motioning for him to continue.

"The second reason is that I will never abandon Lakish. I was the one who hurt her so deeply, so I have an obligation to ensure that she—", He swallowed the words "be happy" mid-sentence, "—will no longer be hurt. This determination is deeply rooted in my heart."

"I see."

Margomedari gently shook his head. "It seems you're sexually repressed."

"You said you wouldn't come to such a conclusion, didn't you?"

"I was just kidding. But I know what kind of person you are. Since you have such a clear course of action, well, then there's no need to worry."

Margomedari gave him a slightly strained smile and patted him on the back. He controlled his strength, of course, but each blow felt powerful enough to break down a plaster wall. Feodor's back ached terribly.

"I've also decided. Leave the problem with the young fairies to me. I won't fail them."

"…Doctor\!"

Feodor's joy was palpable. This was what he had been waiting to hear.

"Is this okay with you, too, Little Nai?"

He turned to the Troll, and she, with a slightly gloomy expression—a look she'd been wearing for the past few days, perhaps it was just her nature—thought for a moment before nodding. "I know. I'll trust you, senior."

"I'm glad."

Their conversation seemed heavy, even lamentable. Feodor, however, was oblivious. The joy of finally finding a positive outcome obscured his attention.

No matter how great one’s mood is, careful preparation is crucial. Feodor wanted to personally confirm the route from his hideout to the harbour area.

On the way, he'd inevitably pass by the Falci Tower Memorial Square (?).

*…But that shouldn't be a problem.*

This is a well-known tourist attraction. Due to its proximity to the harbour area, it attracts a large crowd. Many operas and Image Crystal theatres have also chosen this spot as their stage. For this reason, it seems to be a special place for those who love romance, and many couples of all races choose it as a prime spot for dates. *(That's the problem…)*

It was late at night, the sun setting, and only the dim glow of streetlights illuminated the world. Aside from some nocturnal species, for most people, nighttime was a time for rest. Therefore, the number of pedestrians on the streets decreased, a boon for those who preferred to avoid being seen.

This place, however, seemed to be an exception.

Even at a glance, it was immediately obvious. Every dim corner of the square was filled with a pair of people, stirring up a scene. They were a diverse group of Beastfolk people: dogs, cats, lizards, even pigeons and eagles. They could hardly see at night, and getting here must have been a struggle, but still they were willing to go to such lengths for a romantic evening.

*(They couldn't see around them either, so that shouldn't be a problem.)*

He stepped into the square, trying to attract as little attention as possible.

As he expected, each couple stared intently at their partner, ignoring Feodor, who was walking alone. Indeed, happiness can cloud one's vision, gradually blinding one to many things. Feodor pondered this awkward thought as he walked forward.

In the centre of Falci Memorial Square (?) stood a statue of the Great Sage.

It was said that he was the legendary great man who led many residents of the surface world threatened by the Beasts to the floating islands. He remained somewhere within Regul Aire, watching over the future of this world.

"…If that's the case, then don't just watch, but step up and protect."

After he grumbled this, he immediately felt ashamed.

Delegating the responsibility of protection to capable individuals, taking it for granted, and then blaming the losses on said guardians' incompetence or negligence. This was the typical mindset of the people Feodor despised.

Everyone has their own reasons, their own priorities, something they're willing to sacrifice everything for. And it's normal for others not to know about this. Could it be that what he was about to do was actually meaningless, merely questioning the natural, taken-for-granted existence of this world? Such thoughts occurred even to him, and because he had been absent-mindedly thinking about such things, he realised it too late.

"…Huh?"

"…Ah?"

Right before him, a young girl had also been looking at the statue of the Great Sage.

In the pitch-black night, her bright, grass-coloured hair seemed to gleam.

"How—"

"Why—"

They both opened their mouths, about to cry out in surprise and alarm—but they simultaneously jumped forward and covered each other’s mouths, managing to avoid such a situation.

His mind was in a tizzy. He didn't know why Tiat of all people was here. Although he didn't know, the distance was not good. Tiat also appeared to be dressed in plain clothes and was apparently unarmed. If neither of them was armed, he would have no chance of winning in a fight. 

"You—" He nearly bit Tiat's finger, and managed to pull her hand away. "Why are you in a place like this?" He asked quietly, not wanting to be the centre of attention.

"Do—" His finger was bitten, painfully. "Do I even need to say? I came here chasing after you." Tiat seemed to have the same concerns, and so had lowered her voice.

"…What are you planning this time?"

"You know, right?" he replied.

"I know." she replied.

"Perfect. I'll tell you right now. I've found Dr. Margomedari, and he's agreed to help me. Your little sisters’ lives are no longer in the hands of the Winged Guard."

"Liar." Tiat's eyes widened. "Huh, but I heard it was Naigrat who escaped with that old man."

"She's with us now. I know everything, and she's willing to help me."

He mustered his strength and continued, "There's no need for you to fight or sacrifice your life. No, I'll make that need disappear."

"…You're such an idiot, a truly insane idiot."

Tiat sighed deeply, as if dumbfounded, or perhaps truly speechless.

"Anyway, that's how it is." His gaze drifted elsewhere. "The reason you must obey military orders will soon disappear. You, Collon, Panival, and Lakish won't have to fight the Eleventh Beast—"

"Shh\!"

Suddenly, Tiat lunged.

Was this some kind of combo attack? His entire body tensed reflexively, but contrary to his expectations, Tiat's arms slid around his back, pulling him in, like a lover's embrace.

"Wait… eh… eh?"

"Shh\!"

Since their heights weren't much different, they were now in a position with their lips pressed against each other's ears. Tiat's rapid breathing brushed against Feodor's ear.

"There's a patrol."

Hearing her words, he glanced around. Indeed, there were a few men about to enter the square, and each seemed to be carrying a sword and a musket. They didn't look like they were here to enjoy a tryst with their lovers.

"Winged Guard?" he whispered.

In Falci Memorial Square (?), hugging couples were like the background itself. Since it wouldn't arouse suspicion, this quick-witted tactic was quite appropriate. However, even if it was acting, why would you embrace a man you didn't like just for the sake of disguise? *What’s up with that?*

"They've increased their alertness, their nerves are on edge, and they won't miss even a single sign of trouble. The First Division's policy is different from the Second and Fifth Divisions. They've already issued a wanted poster for you, with some text stating 'injuries don’t matter.' If you were captured now, I think things would be a bit bleak."

"How exactly?"

"An unfortunate accident could happen in the interrogation room."

*…That's certainly a bit bleak.*

"Do you think this is a good idea?"

"It's not. That's why I'm doing this, isn't it? I came to this city to capture you, and now I'm helping you escape. I don't know what I'm doing, but it can't be helped—"

There were footsteps.

They stopped nearby.

Feodor whispered about the danger and quickly put his arms around Tiat's back, hugging her a little tightly. Tiat's whole body trembled, perhaps from fear or nervousness. "Sorry, I feel like they're getting suspicious."

"I know."

They were now embracing each other tightly.

He knew Tiat was trembling slightly. Although she was pretending to be joking, he could sense the suppressed fear within her small frame. This girl was still part of the Winged Guard, having witnessed its current state firsthand. What had she seen, felt, and feared over the past few days?

"That's great."

He sensed Tiat's relief in her quiet words.

"You look so alive. It feels like something terrible is happening every day, so I'm a little scared, wondering if you're injured… maybe even dead."

"So, you’re saying the only one who can capture me is you, and you won’t allow anyone else to do it?”

"Don't be ridiculous, I'm being serious." He was being scolded. "Why… why would you do such a thing?"

After scolding him, Tiat whispered in a sermon-like tone. 

"You're obviously not that strong, and there's no reason you should save us. Why would you do such a dangerous thing?"

"I'm strong, and there are all sorts of reasons to save you. Actually, we've talked about this enough. I don't really like having to re-explain why we have shared interests.”

"But… you might change your mind."

"No. Even if I do, it's only if you change your mind first. If all of you immediately demand better treatment and go on strike, I'll change my mind."

"Well, we're weapons, not soldiers."

"No labour law anywhere says weapons can't go on strike."

Don't think this is an unreasonable twist. The mere fact that weapons can act on their own initiative is abnormal, and they're outside the law. It's simply unreasonable for people who aren't protected by the law to be bound by it. 

He loosened his embrace slightly, cupping Tiat's head in his hands and bringing it to his eyes.

Then their eyes met.

"I simply cannot stand your way of living. Anything or anyone that doesn't value you infuriates me. You yourself are no exception—"

Footsteps sounded nearby.

Approaching.

It was a Winged Guard soldier.

Feodor wondered if he'd just happened to walk around here, or if he'd clearly developed suspicions about them.

*We have to pretend to be a couple*, Feodor thought.

Tiat's face before him seemed a little nervous.

Her eyes wavered.

His lips pressed close.

Their breaths mingled.

At this close distance, the girl closed her eyes.

He didn't know what his body was doing.

For some reason, his mind went blank.

“…”

"…What did you do to me?"

Tiat's voice, almost angry, brought him back to his senses.

The girl, with a slightly blushing face, pouted in dissatisfaction.

"Huh? That’s strange… I just…"

In a matter of seconds, his body lost control of reason. His body acted on its own accord, following its own desires. 

"Do you know where this is? It's in front of the statue of the Great Sage in Falci Memorial Square (?). Legend has it that if two people in love make a vow of eternal love here, they will be blessed with five years of happiness."

—Come to think of it, he seemed to have heard something like this before. While it was romantic, there was no scientific basis for it, so it was probably just superstition.

"You're not used to these kind of sayings, are you?"

"Why do you say that?"

"Because you're not angry."

"It's nothing…" She looked away slightly. “If its not with someone you like, it doesn’t count, right?”

"So this is fine then?"

"If I don’t think this way, I'd strangle you right now."

*Okay, let's just assume it's fine.*

Speaking of which, this girl—when he thought of it—had always admired her cherished senior. That senior was incredibly strong, incredibly perfect, and her life was consumed by a passionate love affair. She probably also longed to spend time like this with some outstanding man, to make a vow of love with him right here, savouring five years of happiness. But that dream had probably been tarnished by him just now.

"How's Lakish? Are you guys together?"

She changed the subject, and Feodor nodded gently in agreement.

"…it just feels… not quite the same."

"That's good. You have to cherish her, okay? She's a little afraid of loneliness, and she'd definitely cry if she were alone."

At this point, something suddenly struck her.

"The sexy stuff should be kept in moderation." She added a rather unnecessary remark.

"I won't do that kind of stuff\! Why are you suddenly acting like a considerate parent right now?" He whispered, as if shouting. It was difficult, but he couldn't help but speak out.

"It's because, while I'm not her parent, I am her older sister."

Tiat was born only a few months before her. This small matter made Tiat proud, and she also asserted her right to love accordingly.

"If a bad guy were to be malicious to her, I certainly wouldn't see it kindly. However, I won't interfere with anything she might wish for. My younger sister's happiness comes first, and I can tolerate other things."

This was truly well-intentioned.

The patrolman's presence slowly faded.

They released each other. A gust of wind swept past, and the lingering warmth on their skin vanished.

Only the memory of a fleeting softness lingered on their lips.

*(—If it's not with someone you like, it doesn’t count.)*

If that's the way it is, then so be it. However, regardless of whether it counted, this incident was still something he couldn't forget anytime soon. At least for him.

…As for Tiat, it was unknown.

Tiat raised her fist. "The Fist That Absolutely Crushes Fatherly Love…”

This mysterious punch was delivered limply, its concentrated force seemingly too weak to crack an egg. It simply poked Feodor's chest.

He felt no pain.

"…It really isn't working, huh."

"What do you mean?"

"Nothing, just a dream."

Tiat uttered this vague reply, then gazed off into the unknown distance.

"It's cold. I'm going back."

She began to walk.

"What I said before is true. Your younger sisters can receive tuning from outside the military. There's no longer any reason, for you and the others, to force yourself to fight."

He caught up and joined her side by side.

"Even if that's the case, it's hard for me to believe it if you're the only one saying it. Besides…"

There was a brief silence. "…Besides what?"

"Well, nothing. More importantly, I'll let you go this time, but the next time I catch up to you, I'll definitely capture you. Remember that." She pointed her index finger at him forcefully.

"…Sorry to disappoint you, but I won't make promises to anyone about meeting again. I've made up my mind on this." He grabbed her finger and moved it in another direction.

"I don't care, just behave and promise that you'll be caught by me next time." Tiat snorted, somehow sounding as if it were a big deal. 

"You, listen more carefully and respect other people's decisions, okay?"

They continued to banter with each other as they headed towards the square's exit.

Feodor suddenly remembered something.

It was the previously mentioned vow of eternal love between two people who pledged their love at the Falci Memorial Square and were granted five years of happiness.

While he was somewhat interested in how the supposed eternity would unfold after the five years, the point wasn't that; it was the happiness during those five years. He wondered what kind of time that represented, exactly.

*(At least—during those 5 years they wouldn’t go onto the battlefield and explode, right?)*

If that explanation was correct, then his earlier actions, or lack thereof, must have been quite regrettable. If they could just use sophistry to convince each other of their mutual affection, and then use their acting to make them vow eternal love, wouldn't Tiat have been able to enjoy five years of happiness?

*(…That's impossible.)*

He shook off those fantasies.

"See you next time\!"

Tiat said, raising a hand energetically.

"Yes, see you next time…"

A tiny fantasy lingered in the corner of his mind, and he instinctively raised his hand in return, the words of a promise to meet again slipping out of his mouth.

He screamed internally and quickly covered his mouth with his hand, but it was too late. Tiat smiled with satisfaction, turned, and ran off into the night. 

"Ah… damn it, I've been tricked."  

He looked up at the sky. She always disrupted his rhythm like this, making it impossible for him to maintain the person he wanted to be.

"That's why I hate you."

 

†

That night, Feodor returned to his hideout.

There was no one inside.

He hadn't expected this. Had his sister come and taken him away? Or had the Winged Guard raided and kidnapped him? Or had Naigrat eaten him?

And then, he quickly realized none of these were true.

There was a letter on the table. "To Feodor" was written in elegant handwriting on the front, and a discreet wax seal was stamped on the back, indicating that it had never been opened.

Feodor cut the seal with a letter opener.

Then he took out the letter and scanned it. "To Mr. Feodor Jessman—"

The words were written in a delicate, small handwriting. It was unclear how that large frame and thick fingers could have written such a font. Anyway, the letter began with this.

"What I just said was not empty words. For the future of the children of the Fairy Warehouse, we intend to do everything in our power. Thank you for your sincerity and kindness so far. And I hope you will be victorious on the battlefield that suits you."

He reread the letter several times, but the content and meaning remained unchanged.

Even when he opened the window and looked out the street, he certainly didn't see the massive figure.

"Is that so… They've resorted to their own methods? It's a bit surprising that they've resorted to such tactics at this point."

He leaned against the wall, muttering with disappointment and exhaustion.

This development wasn't entirely unexpected. However, precisely because the journey so far had been smooth, he truly hoped that it would be as peaceful and stable as possible. But in reality, Margomedari began to act on his own will. He no longer allowed anyone to pull him back, and he trembled with guilt, shrinking his body… no, it was still huge. Feodor had no idea what had caused this change.

"There's really nothing I can do…"

No matter how the situation changed, his purpose remained the same, and what he had to do remained unchanged. After all, he had just promised Tiat that he was certain those fairy children would be safe.

He didn't want to, and couldn't, let that become a lie.

Seeing Lakish sleeping safely in the next room, he breathed a sigh of relief. While he had no doubt those two wouldn’t harm the girl, they could still take her away. Since they hadn't done so, it meant they were prepared to take some kind of risk. And, from now on… or perhaps just for the short term…the girl would be entrusted to Feodor Jessman. "Thank you for your sincerity and kindness so far… huh? You've lived so long, even dealt with my sister before, but you're such an old man, completely ignorant of the dangers of the world. How could the sincerity and kindness of Imps be genuine?"

Indeed, this development wasn't entirely unexpected. He couldn't have failed to account for betrayal, miscalculation, and plan failure. Therefore, he had, of course, already prepared his next move.

This was a second-best strategy, prepared in the event that he couldn't escape the city successfully.

This wasn't the worst possible outcome. While he wasn't confident it would go smoothly, if he acted properly, the rewards would be immense, even greater than a successful escape plan. But honestly, he truly wasn't confident it would go smoothly, and a cold sweat broke out in his heart.

Yes, since there was no escape, there was only one way to go.

It is said that five hundred years ago, the surface of the earth far below began to crumble. Humans went extinct, the Elves went extinct, the Morrighan (earth-dragons?) went extinct, and the Dragons went extinct.

Afterwards and ever since, other races also tried their best to survive, continuing their own desperate struggle. And yet, many lives perished, and many races vanished.

Even after being guided to the floating islands of Regul Aire, the situation did not improve much. Destruction continued to haunt them. The moment anyone ceased their struggle for life, the Deathbringer's bony hand would rest upon their shoulder.

Everyone now lived in this world.

Everyone now struggled in this world.

He squinted at the dark-haired young man reflected in the window.

The angle was poor, so he couldn't see his expression.

So, Feodor curled his lips and smiled to himself.

"Rise to the challenge and seize everything."

He spoke with resolve, declaring his mission.

### **Part 3 – Two Girls Entangled**

Her hazy consciousness suddenly cleared.

At the same time, confusion gripped her body.

Where was this?

Who was I?

She looked around—what she saw was an unfamiliar place. Or rather, a place where she wasn't even sure if it was even a place. From front to back, left to right, and above, was a boundless, blinding darkness. Within this darkness, scattered objects resembled white pottery shards. That whiteness shifted into a rainbow of colours depending on the angle. In this world devoid of any light, those objects were somehow the only ones that were remarkably clear.

And it seemed—where she stood was one of those pottery shards.

The pure white, narrow plain, occupied an area roughly the size of a mansion.

"This… is a dream," she murmured with certainty. This scene was so utterly detached from reality that it was a distinctly lucid dream. She had many things on her mind, but first she decided to pick up a fallen pottery shard at her feet. She reached out, her fingertips touching it.

—Lakish, hurry up, hurry up, come here\!

She instinctively retracted her finger.

She heard a voice. No, it was a replay in her mind. She seemed to see a young girl with grass-coloured hair, waving her hands in the forest. What was that just now? Even as she tried to know the answer to this question, the pottery shard she had touched collapsed before her like sand, sucked into the ground—or rather, the other pottery shards at her feet.

She touched another shard.

—Hehehe, first one to grab it wins\!

She saw another young girl, her mouth wide open, taking a bite of bread.

She touched another shard.

—Haha, that reaction is really typical of you.

Another young girl ran with a look of joy on her face. Her vision followed her back as a small fist appeared in the corner of her vision.

The next piece of pottery… she withdrew her hand before touching it.

She understood several things. These were all the memories of "Lakish", the fairy soldier named Lakish Nyx Seniolis, that had been accumulated since childhood. The girls she saw in her memories—Tiat, Collon, and Panival—were all important friends, family, colleagues, and partners of Lakish.

"Lakish Nyx Seniolis…?"

That should be her name. Feodor, who had held out his hand to her, had told her this name while she, without a name or past, crouched in the rain. And everyone she met before and after that had also addressed her by this name—no, it was this body she had been. She was Lakish, merely losing her memory due to excessive magical exertion (even her personality seemed to have slightly changed). She was still the fairy soldier she'd always been called, and that fact remained unchanged. She had always believed this, and wanted to believe it. She wondered if Feodor knew her inner thoughts, but he always treated her as Lakish. That was why she could rest assured.

However, if this was true, then why didn't she feel a single tinge of nostalgia when she saw the memories of that "Lakish" with her own eyes? It was like reading a stranger's diary, and all she felt was guilt. How could this be?

"Maybe… I'm just overthinking it."

She looked around.

Perhaps it was just a series of bad coincidences. The memories she'd seen so far just didn't connect with her present self, which was why she couldn't understand them. If she looked, there would surely be a memory that would make her feel tangibly like her past. She believed this, and then she looked around. "…That…is…"

Found it.

There was an exceptionally large piece of pottery floating a little way off. And it happened that several of the larger pieces formed a staircase-like path. While it would require some difficult movements, there was no need to spread wings.

When she saw that piece of pottery, she somehow knew it was different from the other pieces, from the other memories. She was certain that the past awakened by touching it was directly connected to her own personality.

She was about to approach it—that moment, her sleeve was pulled.

Turning around, she saw a vague, shimmering figure.

She squinted her eyes to check its appearance. The figure was short, its hair a bright orange, though the colour was hard to discern due to its own luminescence. She seemed about fifteen, and she felt familiar. It was the same face she'd seen in the mirror every morning these days.

"…Lakish."

She called out the name so frankly, it startled even herself.

The light dimmed.

A young girl, looking troubled and frightened, appeared. She looked gentle and vulnerable, giving off a protective vibe. Yet, she also possessed an uncanny tolerance, making it seem as if everyone around her was being protected in return.

"Yes, it's you."

She was certain this girl was the true appearance of Lakish Nyx Seniolis. She was the one Feodor cherished, the one Tiat, Collon, and Panival shared such close memories with. Furthermore, she was most likely a different person from the one standing here. By looking at this face objectively, as if it were someone else's, she could clearly see that.

As she accepted this, she glanced at the girl before her, who seemed to be expressing deep sorrow.

"…Why do you have that expression? Seriously."

She should be the one wanting to cry. This "her," this "someone" with no memories of Lakish and no connection to her, had once again lost everything: her name, the past she'd heard from others… even the reason Feodor cherished her.

He should know all this. Or perhaps he didn't? Either way, she wouldn't be surprised, but either way, she felt desolate.

"Okay\!"

After understanding this, the next step was naturally decided: to confirm the contents of the large pottery fragment, which was undoubtedly connected to her, and awaken herself. Then, she could stand before him with dignity, head held high.

Just as she was about to move forward, her waist was firmly gripped by an entrapping hug.

*—No, no, no, no, you can't go over there—*

She thought she heard a voice.

"Hey, enough\! Let go\! Why are you trying to stop me?"

She pressed down on Lakish's head, trying to pull her away, but Lakish resisted with greater force than she had expected.

"What does it matter? I, unlike you, have nothing. If Lakish is your name, then I don't even have a name for myself\!"

If there was any strong emotion within her, it was her trust in Feodor. But even this was instilled into her nearly blank heart by his own power, his Imp Eyes. In this way, the emotion she had harboured even before she sensed this trust… the true emotion that had been within her from the very beginning, was that unquenchable fire of hatred.

Whatever it took, she wanted to reclaim something she could confidently call her own.

"Sorry\!"

She threw Lakish away with all her might.

Then, she broke into a sprint, using several shards of pottery as stepping stones to leap into the night sky. In one breath, she approached the target shard and reached out.

*—No—*

She ignored the voice, or rather, her thoughts, behind her trying to stop her, and then—

A blazing flame.

It flowed from her fingertips into her body.

"Huh…"

No different from before, the shard of pottery her fingertips touched lost its shape, dissolving into a memory of the past. If anything, it wasn't like reading someone else's diary. She was even certain that this was something she had once owned.

'Continuous wailing' 'Darkness where no stars can be seen' 'Burned remains' 'Regret' 'Eyes of hatred' 'Strong prayers' 'Irreplaceable purpose' 'Night without light' 'She who was once my dear friend' 'Countless hands wrapped around my ankles' 'Prayers that were not delivered' 'Wishes that were not understood' 'Children falling, burning with laughter' 'Falling into a bottomless cave' 'The Cyclops is shouting something' 'A voice, a voice, a voice echoing in my ears' 'A blow from the most ancient Dug Weapon’ 'A strong desire to return' 'Boundless grey desert' 'The Fourteenth Beast of Light' 'A burning heart' 'Burning' 'Burning' 'Burning' 'Burning'

It poured in like a dam bursting—no, it revived from within her. It was fragments, like fragments, blurry images, not sure if they should be called memories. The sheer volume, coupled with a momentum that seemed to wash over her, swept towards her. She immediately regretted ignoring Lakish's advice. Lakish knew that what lay within that pottery shard was definitely not good.

She turned to look behind her. She saw Lakish, her face on the verge of tears, about to run toward her. "I'm so sorry." Though those three words swirled in her mind, the words that came to her lips were: "echoing prayers," "intertwined fingertips," "bound objects of bound wishes," "swallowed by storm clouds," "falling, sinking," "sinking," "sinking," "sinking."

She opened her eyes.

Her heart was beating so fast it felt like it was about to burst.

"…I…"

She pressed her hand against her chest through her shirt, desperately trying to catch her breath.

"I…"

Her breathing and heartbeat gradually calmed down over time.

But the turmoil within her heart wouldn't subside so easily. "I… what exactly is this…"

What exactly was that rush of images? If that really was her past memory, then what kind of person was "my past self"? Was it good, bad, harmful, or…

 

At the table, just the two of them.

"How long can I stay by your side?"

She asked Feodor.

This was the first question she had never asked.

The boy tilted his head, his expression complex, as he pondered for a long moment.

"Until you tire of me."

"In other words, until death does us part, right?"

"Ah… well, if you take it literally, without delving into the underlying meaning, then yes that's it, okay?"

He was shy.

The expression was unexpectedly endearing, and she couldn't help but chuckle.

She had a strong thought. This person deeply cherished Lakish Nyx Seniolis, and so she, too, was cherished. He supported her, and she supported him. She felt frankly happy about it, and there was nothing wrong with accepting it. As long as she had truly been the girl called by that name.

"…"

Indeed, the girl she had met in her dream seemed perfectly suited to this boy. She was a girl who was both suitable to love and to be loved. Feodor was a man of few words (not very frank/blunt?), so she was truly the perfect partner for him.

On the other hand, she herself.

What about a monster like herself, harbouring something like that hatred within?

"Don't you think I'm dangerous?"

"I know, but things have come to this point." He answered readily.

He felt that way, right? Not only had he not stayed away from the explosive Leprechauns, he had even brought her here, so there was no doubt about what he said. Of course, the specifics of the "danger" he imagined might be different from what she feared, but that didn't negate the love in his heart and its preciousness… That was how she felt. She wanted to feel that way.

"Lakish? Did anything happen this morning?"

"No, nothing." She shook her head.

"Dr. Margomedari and his team have launched their operation. From now on, long-held secrets will be revealed one after another, and we'll be quite busy. If you're not feeling well…"

"It's nothing, I told you. Boys who cling too much will be disliked."

"Hmm." Although Feodor couldn't possibly be truly worried about being disliked, he swallowed back any further inquiries.

Yes, for now, she could only rely on this boy's kindness.

He probably wanted Lakish. But the fact was, it was she who stayed here. Until he abandoned her, she would stand by him and be his support.

She was undoubtedly a sinner, condemned for simply existing. So, adding one or two more sins wouldn't matter at this point. That's right, the girl who now bears the name Lakish Nyx Seniolis secretly made up her mind. 

## **Chapter 5 – “-the previous night-” / “The Silent Dead and the Talkative Living”**

![A person holding a childAI-generated content may be incorrect.][image8]

The low hum of the cursed furnace reached this distant room.

For the residents of the nearby village, this might slightly disturb their sleep… Aiseia Myse Valgalis thought absentmindedly. Of course, with few residents around these days, such concerns were likely unnecessary.

The moon in the night sky, visible from the small window, was obscured by a hazy umbrella.

"…What is this?"

She pushed her wheelchair towards the interior.

The high-level operations room. In this small room, heavily protected against espionage, only Aiseia and the guest were present. If you count the person who had been sleeping, there would be three.

"No way—ah, I can't see anything."

A coffin stood in the centre of the room.

A woman in a long robe opened the lid, peered intently at the body within, and then raised her head. Her silver eyes could be seen emitting an eerie glow, then slowly fading, finally dissolving into the darkness.

"Even the power of the Silver Eyes cannot penetrate? Is it because it's sealed or obstructed (?)?"

"No, our wood chip magic (?)… tactical foresight is all about tracing back causes and conditions, drawing future events into view. But when dealing with the dead, who have no future, it's usually unusable."

"This person once claimed to be a 'Beast'. Can't they foresee the attacks of the 'Sixth Beast, Teimerre'?"

"I'm sorry." The woman lifted her loose robe and bowed in apology.

"No, it’s us who should be sorry. We made you come all this way in vain, even asking you to do something as reckless leaving the quarantined Floating Island 5 to this outside—"

"…But there's one thing." The woman suddenly lowered her head, peering into the coffin once more with her silver eyes.

"Hmm, what is it? This guy does look quite pretty when he sleeps, but I wouldn't recommend falling for him. Because, in every sense, it's a dangerous path."

"No, that's not it. It's more of a feeling than a sight…"

*Should I say it? Or shouldn't I?* This hesitation silenced the Silver-Eyed Clan (race? Person of that race) for a moment.

"Please tell me."

"…This guy is indeed dead, frozen in time. He was an actor who finished weaving his own story and disappeared on the other side of the curtain. But, how should I put it… it seems like there's someone else on the other side. And that person is still living their own story… or perhaps, eagerly awaiting the next act."

 

†

 

The wind picked up.

On a hill with a wide view, Aiseia stared blankly at the night sky.

In her hand was a Dug Weapon. It was Valgalis, a sword she could wield, and one that still bears her name… strangely. It was a sword that had been gathering dust in a corner of a warehouse for decades, with no worthy wielder. This time, when she arrived at this floating island, she had secretly altered the documents and brought the sword with her, practically treating it as a personal possession.

"…"

She tried to summon her magic power—but immediately gave up. It wasn't something she could do simply by forcing herself. It was like trying to drink dry sand from a container. Even at the risk of her life, she couldn't create even a moment of brilliance.

"It's really… a bit of a struggle…"

Floating Island 39 was already within sight, and the decisive battle was approaching.

This was a battle with no chance of winning, so it would be better to abandon Floating Island 38 before engaging in a battle that would only bring about sacrifice. Such an option certainly existed. In fact, several people, led by First Officer Limeskin, had been advocating for it. However, this would mean releasing unimpeded the Eleventh Beast into the sky, a creature that would be the size of both Islands 38 and 39 combined. Considering the danger, it's best to do everything we can while we still have a way to resist… Most people think so, so this battle is inevitable.

And it's inevitable that several fairies will die in this battle.

"That Technician officer, what a jerk\! He doted on us so much when he was alive, but now he's dead, he just abandons us."

She uttered this unreasonable complaint.

"Aiseia?”

A voice came from below.

"Aiseia, taking a walk?"

"Ouch, what's wrong, little one?"

Slightly above her knees, a sliver of blue sky appeared. Before she could even wonder what it was, the blue sky sprouted arms and legs and climbed onto Aiseia's thigh.

"Are you here alone? Where are those two, Panival and Collon?"

"Noooooo\!" The blue sky crawled onto her thigh—Riel shook her head in defiance.

A newborn fairy. It's still a nobody yet, and there's no telling what kind of person they will become.

"What did they say about you again? Seriously."

Though spring was almost here, the nights were still a bit chilly. Aiseia wrapped her arms around the warm child, as if to envelop her.

Riel nodded, seemingly content, "Hmm," and buried her head in Aiseia's chest.

"But perhaps this wouldn't be so lonely, compared to looking at the sky alone."

After she told herself this, she suddenly felt the warmth in her arms become incredibly endearing, and couldn't help but hold on tighter.

She had come here originally wanting to be alone. She got out of her wheelchair, sat on the grass, and simply gazed at the sky, lost in memories. However, she couldn't bear being alone, and, as now, she was tended by Riel’s warmth.

"Oh, even I feel so worthless (without potential? Aimless?)."

People often said her smile was untrustworthy.

They also often said she was always smiling, and they couldn't understand her true intentions.

To avoid being told that, she made sure to smile constantly. Smiling when happy and joyful is natural. Laughter is crucial when lonely and distressed. Regarding situations where putting on a serious face can make things better, there were only a few such cases. Regarding situations where smiling, creating a little positivity, can improve them, these situations would always exist, at least. "That's why I should smile, that's why I should smile"—this is what was written in the diary of a girl named "Aiseia." Ever since reading this short passage, Aiseia's life has been filled with this mask-like smile. Therefore, when she occasionally finds herself drawn out into such frankness, she feels extremely embarrassed.

"Aiseia."

"Hmm, what's wrong?"

"It's so warm."

"Is that so…"

She seemed to be about to remember something, tears on the verge of falling.

"That's great… It's worth it to be alive today…"

She looked up at the sky, hiding the growing mist in her eyes.

Then, she heard the child in her arms begin to snore.

"Riel—\! Damn it, where did you go\!"

"Okay, I won't be mad, come out—\! I won't punish you, come out—\!"

Two new voices approached.

There were quite a lot of guests tonight. Aiseia looked over, a little dumbfounded.

"Oh, Aiseia?"

"Oh, just in time, senior, have you seen Riel around here—Ouch\!"

Parting the tall grass, Collon and Panival appeared together.

"Hehehe, what you're looking for is here with me, so be quiet."

Hmm, how could this happen? Collon groaned softly.

"I can't punish her like this," Panival muttered.

"What's wrong with this kid this time?" Aiseia asked, stroking Riel's head.

"I was going to send her to the airship, but she ran off."

As Essia thought about the word "airship," she remembered. "Oh—about sending her to Floating Island 68, right?"

"Yes, it's about time she take refuge in the Fairy Warehouse. It's dangerous here."

Panival was right.

The Winged Guard base in Lyell City and its surroundings were bustling with preparations for the impending battle with the Beast. Piles of steel were being moved to the right, piles of gunpowder to the left.

Someone was so frightened they screamed in terror, while another mishandled their device and caused a prototype weapon to explode. This went far beyond the level of poor parenting. It was bad not only for her mental health but also her physical health. A child shouldn't be left here any longer.

This child should go to the Fairy Warehouse. From now on, she would be raised in an environment filled with love (of whatever kind) under the care of Naigrat… the mother of all fairies.

Those of them here couldn't always be by her side. Because in the battle starting tomorrow, they'll probably disappear one by one—

"What did the child say?"

"She said she didn't want to go, that she wanted to wait for her father to come back… something like that."

"…Father?"

"She was talking about Feodor, I think."

Of course, there was no one else. Even though there was no one else, hearing that word still made her think of someone else.

Somewhere deep inside, deep enough that she couldn't even grasp it, she still relied on him.

"In the end, no matter where we go, our entire race is just spoiled brats…"

She shook her head and looked down at the sleeping face in her arms.

There was no anxiety or resentment, and drool hung at the corner of her mouth.

Riel simply savoured the quiet and peaceful time.
